questions.q: If the density of a mixture of nitrogen and oxygen gases at 400 K and 1 atm pressure is $0.920 \mathrm{gL}^{-1}$, what is the mole fraction of nitrogen in the mixture? $(R=0.082 \mathrm{ L}$ afm $\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{ K}^{-1}$; assume ideal gas behavior for oxygen and nitrogen)
questions.solution:
Given \rightarrow $\mathrm{P}=$1 $\mathrm{~atm}$\begin{aligned}
& $\mathrm{T}=$400 $\mathrm{~K}$ \\
& $\text{ Density }$(\delta)=0.920 $\mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$ \\
& $\mathrm{R}=$0.082 $\mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~atm} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$ \\
& $\mathrm{~V}=$1 $\mathrm{~L}$
\end{aligned}$
The molar mass can be found using the density and the ideal gas law
$M=$\frac{\delta R T}{P}$ \qquad ...$\mathrm{(i)}$
Futting the value in equation (i)
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{M}=\frac{0.920 \times 0.082 \times 400}{1} \\
& \mathrm{M}=30.016 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
Let $x$ be the mole fraction of $\mathrm{N}_2 and (1-\mathrm{x})$ be the mole fraction of oxygen $\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)$
The molar masses of nitrogen and oxygen are
$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{N}_2}=28 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}_2}=32 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
mole fraction.
$($\mathrm{M}$)=$\mathrm{x}$ \cdot $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{N}_2}+$(1 \cdot-$\mathrm{x}$) \cdot $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}_2}
Substituting$ the values$\begin{aligned}
& 30.016=x .28+(1-x) .32 \\
& 30.016=28 x+32-32 x \\
& 4 x=32-30.016 \\
& 4 x=1.984 \\
& x=1.984 / 4=0.496 \approx 0.456
\end{aligned}$
The mole fraction of nitrogen in mixture is approximately
$0.496 \approx 0.456$

questions.q: A vessel of volume $24.6 \mathrm{ L}$ contains 1.5 moles of $\mathrm{H}_2$ and 2.5 moles of $\mathrm{N}_2$ at $300 \mathrm{ K}$. Calculate the partial pressure of $\mathrm{N}_2$ in the vessel.
questions.solution:
Partial pressure In a mixture of gases, each constituent gas has a partial pressure, which is the notional pressure of that constituent gas, if it alone occupied the entire volume of the original mixture at the same temperature.
Dalton's law Total pressure of an ideal gas mixture is the sum of the partial pressure of the gases in the mixture.
Partial pressure due to $n_1= \left($p^{{}^{\circ}}{ }_1=$\frac{n_1 R T}{V}\right)
Similarly, due to $n_2= $\left(p_2^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{n_2 R T}{V}\right)$

Given, total volume $=24.6 \mathrm{~L}$
Moles of $\mathrm{H}_2=1.5 \mathrm{~mol}$
Moles of $\mathrm{N}_2=2.5 \mathrm{~mol}$
Temperature $=300 \mathrm{~K}$
Partial pressure of $\mathrm{N}_2=$ ?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Root mean square $(\mathrm{rms})$ speed of $\mathrm{O}_2$ is $500 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ at a constant temperature. Calculate the rms speed and the average kinetic energy of $\mathrm{H}_2$ at the same temperature. (Consider, $\left.R=8.33 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)$
questions.solution:
Given, root mean square $(\mathrm{rms})$ speed of $\mathrm{O}_2$ is
$500 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ at a constant temperature.
Root mean square speed in given by the following expression
$u_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M w}}$
For $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas, $u_{\mathrm{Tms}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\right)}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M w_{\mathrm{H}_2}}} \left(M w\right.$ of $\left.\mathrm{H}_2=2 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}\right)$
For $\mathrm{O}_2$ gas, $u_{\mathrm{rms}\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M w_{\mathrm{O}_2}}} \left(M w\right.$ of $\left.\mathrm{O}_2=32 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}\right) \frac{u_{\mathrm{rms}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\right)}}{u_{\mathrm{rms}\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M w_{\mathrm{H}_2}}} \times \sqrt{\frac{M w_{\mathrm{O}_2}}{3 R T}}$
(Temperature constant, $R=8.33 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ )
$\begin{aligned}
u_{\mathrm{rms}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\right)} & =\sqrt{\frac{M w_{\mathrm{O}_2}}{M w_{\mathrm{H}_2}}} \times u_{\mathrm{rms}\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)}=\sqrt{\frac{32}{2}} \times 500 \\
& =2000 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
Average kinetic energy of $\mathrm{H}_2$ can be calculate as
$=\frac{1}{2} m u^2 \begin{aligned}
{\left[u=2000 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, m=\mathrm{H}_2=2 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}=0.002 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{mol}\right] } \\
=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.002 \times(2000)^2 \\
=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{1000} \times 2000 \times 2000 \\

questions.q:
Which of the following describes an ideal gas?
(i) The volume occupied by a gas molecule is negligible.
(ii) The collision between ideal gases are elastic.
(iii) Particles are very small compared to the distance between each other.
questions.solution:
(i), (ii), (iii)
All gases are made up of a very large number of extremely small particles called molecules. All the molecules of a particular gas are identical in mass and size. The molecules are separated from one another by large space. Hence, the actual volume occupied by the molecules is negligible as compared to the total volume of the gas.
The collisions of gas particles with one another and with the walls of the container are perfectly elastic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The vapour pressure of pure $\mathrm{CCl}_4$ (molar mass $=154 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ ) and $\mathrm{SnCl}_4$ (molar mass $=170 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ ) at $25^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ are 115.0 and 238.0 torr respectively. Assuming ideal behaviour, calculate the total approximate vapour pressure in torr of a solution containing $10 \mathrm{ g}$ of $\mathrm{CCl}_4$ and $15 \mathrm{ g}$ of $\mathrm{SnCl}_4$.
questions.solution:
Given, vapour pressure of pure $\mathrm{CCl}_4$ at $25^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\left(p_{\mathrm{CCl}_4$}^{{}^{\circ}}\right)=115.0 $\text{ torr }$Vapour pressure of pure $\mathrm{SnCl}_4$ at $25^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\left(p_{\mathrm{SnCl}_4$}^{{}^{\circ}}\right)=238.0 $\text{ torr }$Molar mass of $\mathrm{CCl}_4\left[M_{\left(\mathrm{CCl}_4\right)}\right]=154 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
Molar mass of $\mathrm{SnCl}_4\left[M_{\mathrm{SnCl}_4}\right]=170 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
Mass of $\mathrm{CCl}_4$ in solution $\left(w_{\mathrm{CCl}_4}\right)=10 \mathrm{~g}$
Mass of $\mathrm{SnCl}_4$ in solution $\left(w_{\mathrm{SnCl}_4}\right)=15 \mathrm{~g}$
From Dalton's law of partial pressure,
$p_{\text{total }}=\chi_{\mathrm{CCl}_4} \cdot p^{{}^{\circ}}{ }_{\mathrm{CCl}_4}+\chi_{\mathrm{SnCl}_4} \cdot p^{{}^{\circ}}{ }_{\mathrm{SnCl}_4} and
\chi=\frac{n_{\text{simple }}}{n_{\text{total }}}=\frac{w}{M \times n_{\text{total }}}$
Now, $\quad n=\left[\frac{w}{M}\right]_{\mathrm{CCl}_4}=\frac{10}{154}=0.065$ and $\left[\frac{w}{M}\right]_{\mathrm{SnCl}_4}=\frac{15}{170}=0.09$
Thus,
$\begin{aligned} \chi_{\mathrm{CCl}_4} & =\frac{n_{\mathrm{CCl}_4}}{n_{\mathrm{CCl}_4}+n_{\mathrm{SnCl}_4}} \\ & =\frac{0.065}{0.06+0.09} \\ \chi_{\mathrm{CCl}_4} & =\frac{0.065}{0.15}=0.43\end{aligned}$
Therefore,
$\chi_{\mathrm{SnCl}_4}=1-0.43=0.57$
Thus,
$\begin{aligned} p_{\text{total }} & =0.43 \times 115.00+0.57 \times 238 \\ & =49.45+135.66 \\ & =185.11 \approx 185.85 \text{ torr }\end{aligned}$
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

For& $' n '$~moles of a real gas, it can be written as,

$\left(P + \dfrac{an2}{V2}\right)\left(V - nb\right) = nRT$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the approximate most probable velocity of oxygen? If the kinetic energy of one mole of oxygen is $3741.3 \mathrm{ J}$.
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy $(\mathrm{KE})=\frac{3}{2} R T \begin{aligned}\text{ where, }$ R & =$\text{ gas constant }$\\
T & =$\text{ temperature }$\\
\therefore \quad R T & =$\frac{2}{3}(\mathrm{KE})
\end{aligned}$ Most probable velocity (MP) $=\sqrt{\frac{2 R T}{M}}$
where, $M=$ molecular mass of oxygen $=32$
Given $\Rightarrow \mathrm{KE}=3741.3 \mathrm{ J}$
Substituting the value of $R T$ from Eq. (i), we have, $\begin{aligned}\mathrm{MP}$& =$\sqrt{\frac{2 \times 2(\mathrm{KE})}{3 \times M}}$\\
& =$\sqrt{\frac{2 \times 2 \times 3741.3}{3 \times 32} \times 1000}$\\
=$\sqrt{155.88 \times 1000}$& =$\sqrt{155887 \mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ kg}^{-1}}
\end{aligned}$ Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $12 \mathrm{ cm}^3$ of $\mathrm{SO}_2(g)$ diffused through a porous membrane in 1 minute. Under similar conditions $120 \mathrm{ cm}^3$ of another gas diffused in 5 minutes. The molar mass of the gas in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is
questions.solution:
According to law of diffusion rate $(r) \alpha \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$ (molar mass) and $r$ (rate) $\alpha \frac{\text{ volume }(V)}{\text{ time }(t)}$
i.e. $\quad \frac{r_{\left(\mathrm{SO}_2\right)}}{r_{(z)}}=\frac{(V / t)_{\left(\mathrm{SO}_2\right)}}{(V / t)_{(z)}}=\frac{[\mathrm{l} / \sqrt{M}]_{\left(\mathrm{SO}_2\right)}}{(\mathrm{l} / \sqrt{M})_{C_z}}$ or, $\quad \frac{V_{\left(\mathrm{SO}_2\right)} \times t_{(z)}}{V_{(z)} \times t_{\left(\mathrm{SO}_2\right)}}=\sqrt{\frac{M_{(z)}}{M_{\left(\mathrm{SO}_2\right)}}}$
Given, $\begin{aligned} V_{\left(\mathrm{SO}_{2}\right)} & =12 \mathrm{ cm}^3 \\
t_{\left(\mathrm{SO}_{2}\right)} & =1 \text{ minute }=1 \times60=60 \mathrm\sec\\
V_{(z)} & =120 \mathrm{ cm}^3 \\
t_{(z)} & =5 \text{ minutes }=5 \times60=300 \mathrm\sec
\end{aligned}$ and molar mass $(M) of \mathrm{SO}_2=32+(2 \times 16)=64$
Thus, $\frac{12 \times 300}{120 \times 60}=\sqrt{\frac{M_z}{64}}$ or, $\frac{1}{4}=\frac{M_z}{4}\therefore \quad M_z=\frac{64}{4}=16$ Hence, molar mass of given gas is $=16 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$

questions.q: The wavenumber of first spectral line of Lyman series of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ ion is $x \mathrm{ m}^{-1}$. What is the wavenumber (in $\mathrmm^{-1}$ ) of second spectral line of Balmer series of $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$ ion?
questions.solution:
For Lyman $\begin{aligned} & \overline{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \times \mathrm{Z}^2\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}\right] \\ & =\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \times 2^2\left[\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}\right] \\ & =\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \times 4 \times \frac{3}{4} \\ & \overline{\mathrm{v}}=3 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=\mathrm{x} \\ & \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{3}...(i) \end{aligned}$
For Balmer series $\begin{aligned} & \overline{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \times 3^2 \times\left[\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{4^2}\right] \\ & =\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} 9 \times \frac{3}{16}. \end{aligned}$
Putting the value of $R_H$ from eq. (i) $\bar{v}=\frac{x}{3} \times 9 \times \frac{3}{16}=\frac{9 x}{16}$

questions.q: The threshold frequency of a metal is $10^{15} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$. The ratio of maximum kinetic energies of the photoelectrons, when the metal is made to strike with radiations of frequencies $1.5 \times 10^{15} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$ and $2.0 \times 10^{15} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$ respectively is
questions.solution:
$v_0=1.0 \times 10^{15} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$
Maximum kinetic energy will be at the highest frequencies and when all the energy is utilized for the kinetic energy of the ejected electrons:
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E}_1=\mathrm{h}\left(v_1-v_0\right) \\
& =6.626 \times 10^{-34}\left(1.5 \times 10^{15}-1.0 \times 10^{15}\right) \\
& =6.626 \times 10^{-34}\left(0.5 \times 10^{15}\right) \\
& =3.313 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{ J} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{K}_{.} \mathrm{E}_2=\mathrm{h}\left(v_2-v_0\right) \\
& =6.626 \times 10^{-34}\left(2.0 \times 10^{15}-1.0 \times 10^{15}\right) \\
& =6.626 \times 10^{-34}\left(1 \times 10^{15}\right) \\
& =6.626 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{ J}
\end{aligned}$
Thus, the ratio will be :
$\frac{\mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E}_1}{\mathrm{ K} . \mathrm{E}_2}=\frac{3.313 \times 10^{-19}}{6.626 \times 10^{-19}}=1: 2$

$\left(h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\right)$
questions.solution:
Given : - Kinetic energy $=2 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J}$
Radiation of frequency $=1.0 \times 10^{15} \mathrm{~Hz}\mathrm{h}=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}$
According to Einstein's equation
Kinetic energy $=1 / 2 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{V}^2=\left(\mathrm{V}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}}\right) \qquad ...\mathrm{(1})\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}=$ mass of electron
$\mathrm{V}=$ Frequency of incident radiation
$V_0=$ Threshold Frequency
Putting the value in equation (1)
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 \times 10^{-19}=6.62 \times 10^{-34}\left(1.0 \times 10^{15}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}}\right) \\
& \frac{2 \times 10^{-19}}{6.62 \times 10^{-34}}=1.0 \times 10^{15}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}} \\
& \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{o}}=1.0 \times 10^{15}-0.302 \times 10^{15} \\
& \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{o}}=0.698 \times 10^{15} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}=6.98 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$

$\left(h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\right)$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{x} \cdot \Delta \mathrm{p}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{4 \pi} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{x} \cdot \mathrm{m} \Delta \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{4 \pi} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{4 \pi \cdot \Delta \mathrm{x} \cdot \mathrm{m}}=\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{ J} . \mathrm{S}}{4 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-33} \mathrm{ m} \times 10 \mathrm{ g}} \\ & \Delta v=0.52 \times 10^{-34} \times 10^{33} \times 10^{-1} \mathrm{ kg} \mathrm{ m}^2 \mathrm{ s}^{-1} \times \mathrmm^{-1} \times \mathrmg^{-1} \\ & =0.52 \times 10^{-2} \times 10^3 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ s}^{-1} \times \mathrmg^{-1} \\ & =0.52 \times 10 \mathrm{ m} \mathrm{ s}^{-1} \\ & 52.5 \times \frac{\mathrm{x}}{100}=0.52 \times 10\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & x=\frac{0.52 \times 1000}{52.5} \\ & x=9.9 \approx 10\end{aligned}$

According to Heisenberg
$\Delta x \times m \times \Delta v=\frac{h}{4 \pi}$
where $\Delta x=$ uncertainty in position.
$m=$ mass of particle
$\Delta v=$ uncertainty in velocity
According to question
$\Delta x_A \times m \times 0.05=\frac{h}{4 \pi}\ldots(1)\Delta x_B \times 5 m \times 0.02=\frac{h}{4 \pi}\ldots(2)$
Eq. (1) divided by Eq. (2), then
$\frac{\Delta x_A \times m \times 0.05}{\Delta x_B \times 5 m \times 0.02}=1$
or $\frac{\Delta x_A}{\Delta x_B}=2$

questions.solution:
According to Bohr's concept, an electron always move in the orbit with angular momentum (m v r)$ equal to $n h / 2 \pi$.
\therefore \quad m v r=\frac{n h}{2 \pi}$
or
$r=\frac{n}{2 \pi} \cdot\left(\frac{h}{m v}\right) \text{ or } r=\frac{n \lambda}{2 \pi}$
(From de -Broglie equation, $\lambda=\frac{h}{m v}$ )
for fourth orbit $n=4\begin{gathered}
r=\frac{2 \lambda}{\pi} \\
\therefore \text{ circumference }=2 \pi r=2 \pi \times \frac{2 \lambda}{\pi}=4 \lambda
\end{gathered}$

questions.solution:
$Freundlich isotherm.
\begin{aligned} & \ln \frac{x}{m}=\ln k+\frac{1}{n} \ln p \\ & \text{ or, } \log \frac{x}{m}=\log k+\frac{1}{n} \log p \\ & y=c+m x \\ & \text{ Slope }(m)=\frac{1}{n} \quad \therefore \quad \frac{1}{n}=0.5 \\ & \text{ Intercept }(\mathrm{c})=\log k=1 \\ & \text{ Pressure }(p)=100 \text{ atm } \\ & \therefore \log \frac{x}{m}=1+0.5 \log 10^2 \\ & \log \frac{x}{m}=1+0.5 \times 2 \Rightarrow \log \frac{x}{m}=2 \\ & \frac{x}{m}=10^2=100\end{aligned}$

(A) Adsorption is accompained by decrease in enthalpy as well as in entropy of the system $\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S$ and adsorption is an exothermic process [ thus has $\Delta H=(-)$ ve, i.e. decreases] and randomness, i.e. ( $\Delta$ S) also decreases because after adsorption free movement is restricted, but to make the $\Delta G(-)$ ve, $\Delta H > T$. $\Delta S$. Hence, the statement (A) is correct.
(B) Gases, which can react strongly with adsorbent show chemisorption as they form chemical bonds with the adsorbent. Hence, the statement (c) is also correct.
(C) When the value of slope of the Freundlich isotherm is non-zero, adsorption of a gas depends on pressure over it, till the adsorption is possible. According to Freundlich isotherm equation :
$\frac{x}{m}=k \cdot p^{1 / n}$
where,
$x=$ mass of gas adsorbed,
$m=$ mass of adsorbent,
$p=$ pressure,
$k=$ constant,
$n=$ integer number,
Hence, statement (C) is not correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A micelle formed during the cleansing action by soap is
options: aggregated particles of soap and dirt
an aggregated particle of dust and water
questions.solution: Soap contains hydrophobic (ie, fat soluble or water repelling) as well as hydrophilic (water soluble) end. Hydrophobic end remains soluble in dust or grease particles while hydrophilic end is attracted towards water. Hence, several hydrophobic pocket surrounds the grease particles. This aggregate of soap and dirt is called micelle. On washing with plenty of water dust is removed along with soap.

The $\Delta_f \mathrmH^{{}^{\circ}}$ of $\mathrm{AO}(\mathrm{s}), \mathrm{BO}_2(\mathrm{~g}) and \mathrm{ABO}_3(\mathrm{~s})$ is -635, x and $-1210 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively. $\mathrm{ABO}_3(\mathrm{~s}) \rightarrow \mathrm{AO}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{BO}_2(\mathrm{~g}) ; \Delta_r \mathrmH^{{}^{\circ}}=175 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{ABO}_3(\mathrm{ s}) \rightarrow \mathrm{AO}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{BO}_2(\mathrm{ g}) \Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrmH^{{}^{\circ}}=175 \\ \therefore \quad & \Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrmH^{{}^{\circ}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^0\left(\mathrm{AO}+\mathrm{BO}_2\right)-\Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrmH^{\mathrm{o}}\left(\mathrm{ABO}_3\right) \\ & \Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{H}^0=\Delta_{\mathrm{P}} \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{AO}^0+\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{BO}_2}^0-\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{ABC}_3}^{\mathrm{o}} \\ & 175=-635+\mathrm{x}-(-1210) \\ & 175+635=\mathrm{x}+1210 \\ & \mathrm{x}=-400.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: At $300 \mathrm{~K}, 3.0$ moles of an ideal gas at 3.0 atm pressure is compressed isothermally to one half of its volume by an external pressure of 6.0 atm . The work done (in kJ ) is $\left(\right.$ Given, $\left.\mathrm{R}=0$.082 $\mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~atm}\mathrm{~K}^{-1}\mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$\right)$(1 \mathrm{~L}\mathrm{~atm}=$101.3 $\mathrm{~J})$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{For ideal gas, } \\ & \text{Mole }=3 \\ & \text{Temp }=300 \mathrm{ K} \\ & \text{Pressure }=3 \mathrm{ atm} \\ & \text{PV }=\mathrm{nRT} \\ & \mathrm{V}=\frac{\mathrm{nRT}}{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{ mole} \times 0.082 \mathrm{c} \mathrm{atm} \mathrm{K}^{-1} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1} \times 300 \mathrm{ K}}{3 \mathrm{ atm}} \\ & \mathrm{ V}_1=24.6 \mathrm{ L} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{ V}_2=\frac{\mathrm{V}_1}{2}=\frac{24.6}{2}=12.3 \\ & \Delta \mathrm{ V}=\mathrm{V}_2-\mathrm{V}_1 \\ & =12.3-24.6 \\ & \Delta \mathrm{ V}=-12.3 \mathrm{ L} \\ & \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{ext}}=6 \mathrm{ atm} \\ & \mathrm{ W}=-\mathrm{P}_{\text{ext }}(\Delta \mathrm{V}) \\ & =-6 \times(-12.3) \mathrm{atm} \mathrm{L} \\ & =73.8 \mathrm{ atm} \mathrm{ L} \\ & \mathrm{ Win} \mathrm{kJ}=\frac{73.8 \times 101.3 \mathrm{ kJ}}{1000} \\ & \mathrm{ W}=7.476 \mathrm{ kJ} .\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If $4+3 x-7 x^2$ attains its maximum value $M$ at $x=\alpha$ and $5 x^2-2 x+1$ attains its minimum value $m$ at $x=\beta$, then
$\frac{28(M-\alpha)}{5(m+\beta)}=$
questions.solution:
Let $f(x)=4+3 x-7 x^2\begin{aligned} & f^{\prime}(x)=3-14 x=0 \Rightarrow x=\frac{3}{14}=\alpha \\ & f^{\prime \prime}(x)=-14 < 0 \end{aligned}\therefore f(x)$ is maximum at $x=\frac{3}{14}$ and maximum Value is $f\left(\frac{3}{14}\right)=4+\frac{9}{14}-\frac{63}{196}=\frac{847}{196}=M And g(x)=5 x^2-2 x+1g^{\prime}(x)=10 x-2=0 \Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{5}=\betag^{\prime \prime}(x)=10>0\therefore g(x)$ is minimum at $x=\frac{1}{5}$ and minimum value is $g\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)=5 \times \frac{1}{25}-\frac{2}{5}+1=\frac{4}{5}=m$
Now, $\frac{28(M-\alpha)}{5(m+\beta)}=\frac{28\left(\frac{847}{196}-\frac{3}{14}\right)}{5\left(\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{5}\right)}=\frac{115}{5}=23$.

questions.q: An angle between the curves $x^2-y^2=4$ and $x^2+y^2=4 \sqrt{2}$ is
questions.solution:
$x^2-y^2=4$ ...(i)
$x^2+y^2=4 \sqrt{2}$ ...(ii)
Adding both equations,
$\begin{aligned} & x^2=2(1+\sqrt{2}) \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{2} \sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1} \\ & \therefore \quad y^2=2(\sqrt{2}-1) \Rightarrow y=\sqrt{2} \sqrt{\sqrt{2}-1}\end{aligned}$
Differentiating both (i) and (ii)
$\begin{aligned} & 2 x-2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x}{y}=m_1 \\ & \text{ and } 2 x+2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-x}{y}=m_2 \\ & \tan \theta=\left|\frac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1 m_2}\right|=\left|\frac{\frac{x}{y}+\frac{x}{y}}{1-\frac{x^2}{y^2}}\right| \\ & \quad=\left|^{2} \frac{x}{y} \times \frac{y^2}{y^2-x^2}\right|=\left|\frac{2 x y}{y^2-x^2}\right|=\left|\frac{4}{-4}\right|=1 . \\ & \therefore \quad \theta=\frac{\pi}{4} .\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The maximum volume (in cu. units) of the cylinder which can be inscribed in a sphere of radius 12 units is
questions.solution:
$12^2=r^2+\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)^2$
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow V=\pi r^2 h \\ & \Rightarrow V=\pi\left(144-\frac{h^2}{4}\right) h \\ & \Rightarrow V=144 \pi h-\frac{\pi}{4} h^3 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d V}{d h}=144 \pi-\frac{3 \pi}{4} h^2\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d V}{d h}=0 \Rightarrow 144 \pi=\frac{3 \pi}{4} h^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad h^2=48 \times 4 \Rightarrow h=8 \sqrt{3} \\ & \therefore \quad 12^2=r^2+48 \Rightarrow r^2=96\end{aligned}$ Volume $=\pi r^2 h=\pi \times 96 \times 8 \sqrt{3}=768 \sqrt{3} \pi \mathrm{cm}^3$.

Differentiate both sides w.r.t a $2 b c \sin A S A=-20 \delta a\Rightarrow \delta_E=\frac{b c \sin \mathrm{ A} \mathbb{A}}{a}$..(i) Area $(\Delta)=\frac{1}{2} \times b c \times \sin \mathrm{A}$..(ii) $\frac{\mathbb{C}}{\sin A}=2 R$..(iii) From (i), (ii) and (iii) $\delta a=\frac{2 \Delta \times \delta A}{2 R \sin A}$ Percentage error $=\frac{\delta a}{a} \times 100=\frac{\Delta \delta \mathrm{A}}{2 \mathrm{R}^2 \sin ^2 \mathrm{ A}} \times 100$

questions.solution:
Let $f(x)=\sec x \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=\sec x \tan x$
Take $a=60^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $h=-1^{{}^{\circ}}=-0.0174$ Then $f(a)=\sec 60^{{}^{\circ}}=2 \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(a)=2 \sqrt{3}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow f(a+h) \approx f(a)+h \cdot f^{\prime}(a) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad f\left(59^{{}^{\circ}}\right) \\ & =\sec 59^{{}^{\circ}}=\sec 60^{{}^{\circ}}-(0.0174)(2 \sqrt{3}) \\ & \\ & =2-0.0602736 \Rightarrow \sec 59^{{}^{\circ}}=1.9397 \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If Rolle's Theorem is applicable for the function $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}x^p \log x, & x \neq 0 \\ 0, & x=0\end{array}\right.$ on the interval $[0,1]$, then a possible value of $p$ is
questions.solution:
Rolle's theorem is applicable on $f(x)\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow f(x) \text{ is continuous on }[0,1] \\ & \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)=0 \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} x^p \log ^x=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\log x}{x^{-p}}=0 \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\frac{1}{x}}{-p x^{-p-1}}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x^p}{-p}=0\end{aligned}$
Only possible when $p>0 \Rightarrow p=1$

questions.q: Let $m$ be the slope of the normal $L$ drawn at $(1,2)$ to the curve $x=t^2-7 t+7, y=t^2-4 t-10$ and $a x+b y+c=0$ be the equation of the normal L. If G.C.D of $(a, b, c)$ is 1 , then $m(a+b+c)=$

& t=1,6 \\

& t=6,-2
\end{aligned} $\therefore t=6$ is common solution \therefore \text{ Slope of normal }=\frac{7-2(6)}{2(6)-4}=\frac{-5}{8}$ Equation of normal : $y-2=\frac{-5}{8}(x-1) \begin{aligned}& 8 y-16=-5 x+5 \\
& 5 x+8 y-21=0 \\

$

questions.q: If the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{xe}^{-\mathrm{x}}, \mathrm{x} \in \mathbb{R}$ attains its maximum value $\beta$ at $x=\alpha$ then $(\alpha, \beta)=$
questions.solution:
$f(x)=x \cdot e^{-x} \begin{aligned}& f^{\prime}(x)=-x \cdot e^{-x}+e^{-x} \\
& =e^{-x}(1-x) \\
& f^{\prime}(x)=0 \Rightarrow x=1 \\
& \text{$ and $} f^{\prime \prime}(x)=x \cdot e^{-x}-e^{-x}-e^{-x}=x e^{-x}-2 e^{-x} \\
& \because f^{\prime \prime}(1)=\frac{1}{e}-\frac{2}{e}< 0
\end{aligned}$\therefore$ maxima is attained at $x=1 \begin{gathered}$ f(x)_{\max }=1 $\cdot$ e^{-1}=\frac{1}{e}$\\
\therefore($\alpha, \beta) \equiv\left(1, \frac{1}{e}\right)
\end{gathered}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the absolute maximum and absolute minimum values of the function. $f(x)=x^3-2 x^2+x-3$ defined on $[0,2]$ are $\mathrm{M}$ and $\mathrm{m}$ respectively, then $\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}=$
questions.solution:
$f(x)=x^3-2 x^2+x-3$
f^{\prime}(x)=3 x²-4 x+1 $\begin{aligned} \text{$ and $} f^{\prime}(x)=0 \Rightarrow 3 x²-4 x+1=0 \\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow 3 x²-3 x-x+1=0 \Rightarrow(3 x-1)(x-1)=0 \\ \text{ and } \therefore \quad x=\frac{1}{3},1
\end{aligned}$ \\ $\begin{aligned} & f^{\prime \prime}(x)=6 x-4 \\ & f^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) < 0 \Rightarrow \text{ Maxima } \\ & f^{\prime \prime}(1) > 0 \Rightarrow \text{ Minima } \\ & f(0)=-3 \text{$ and $} f(2)=8-8+2-3=-1 \\ & f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{1}{27}-\frac{2}{9}+\frac{1}{3}-3=\frac{-77}{27} \\ & f(1)=1-2+1-3=-3 \\ & \therefore \quad \text{ Absolute } \max =-1=M \\ & \quad \text{ Absolute } \min =-3=m \\ & \therefore \quad M+m=-3-1=-4.\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a line having slope 2 is a tangent to the curve $y=x^4-6 x^3+13 x^2-12 x+5$ at points $P  \left(x_1, y_1\right)$ and $Q\left(\mathrm{x}_{2}, \mathrm{y}_{2}\right), \mathrm{x}_{1}, \mathrm{x}_{2} \in \mathrm{N}$ then $\mathrm{x}_{1} \mathrm{x}_{2}- \mathrm{y}_{1} \mathrm{y}_{2}=$
questions.solution: $y=x^4-6 x^3+13 x^2-10 x+5\begin{aligned} & \text{ Slope$ of $tangent }=\frac{d y}{d x}=4 x^3-18 x^2+26 x-10 \\ & \because \frac{d y}{d x}=2 \\ & 4 x^3-18 x^2+26 x-10=2 \\ & (x-1)(x-2)(2 x-3)=0 \\ & \therefore 2 \text{ points can be taken as } x=1 \text{ and } x=2 \\ & \text{ if } x_1=2 \\ & y_1=(2)^4-6(2)^3+13(2)^2-10(2)+5=5 \\ & \text{ when } x_2=1 \\ & y_2=(1)^4-6(1)^3+13(1)^2-10(1)+5=3 \\ & \therefore x_1 x_2-y_1 y_2=(1 \times 2)-(3 \times 5)=-13\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The diameter of a sphere is measured as $42 \mathrm{ cm}$. If there is an error of $1 / 77 \mathrm{ cm}$ in measuring it, then the error involved in the volume of that sphere (in cubic centimeters) is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & d=42 \mathrm{ cm} ; r=21 \mathrm{ cm} \\ & V=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \text{$ and $} \Delta V=\left(\frac{d}{d r} v\right) \times \Delta r \\ & \Rightarrow \Delta V=\frac{d}{d r}\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3\right) \Delta r \Rightarrow \Delta V=\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi \times 3 r^2\right) \Delta r \\ & \Rightarrow \Delta V=4 \pi r^2 \Delta r \Rightarrow \Delta V=4 \times \frac{22}{7}(21)^2 \times \frac{1}{77 \times 2} \\ & \therefore \Delta v=36.\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
$x$ and $y$ are two positive integers such that $2 x+3 y=50$.
If $x^2 y^3$ is maximum for $x=\alpha$ and $y=\beta$, then $\frac{\alpha}{2}+\frac{\beta}{5}=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}& \text2 x+3 y=50 \\
& P=x² y³ \text{ (given) }\\
& \Rightarrow P=x²\left(\frac{50-2 x}{3}\right)^3 \Rightarrow P=\frac{1}{27} x^2(50-2 x)^3 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d P}{d x}=\frac{1}{27}\left[ x^2 \cdot3(50-2 x)^2(-2)+2 x \cdot(50-2 x)^3\right] \\
& \text{ when } \frac{d P}{d x}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow-6 x²(50-2 x)^2+2 x(50-2 x)^3=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x(50-2 x)^2[-3 x+50-2 x]=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x(50-2 x)^2(50-5 x)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x=0,25,10 \Rightarrow \therefore y=\frac{50}{3},0,10
\end{aligned} Clearly$ for max. value of P, x=10, y=10$
\therefore \quad \frac{\alpha}{2}+\frac{\beta}{5}=\frac{10}{2}+\frac{10}{5}=7
$

questions.q: Electric current (I) is measured by galvanometer, the current being proportional to the tangent of the angle $(\theta)$ of deflection. If the deflection is read as $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ and an error of $1 \%$ is made in reading it, the percentage error in the current is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \quad I \propto \tan \theta \\ & d I=\sec ^2 \theta d \theta \\ & \frac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100=\sec ^2 \theta \frac{\Delta \theta}{\theta} \times 100 \\ & \text{ when } \theta=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \frac{\Delta \theta}{\theta} \times 100=\frac{\pi}{4} \times \frac{1}{100} \times 100=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100=\left[\sec ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right] \times \frac{\pi}{4}=2 \times \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the function $\int(x)=\frac{x}{5}+\frac{5}{x},(x \neq 0)$ attains its relative maximum value at $\mathrm{x}=a$ then $\sqrt{a^2+2 a-6}=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\frac{x}{5}+\frac{5}{x}=\frac{x^2+25}{5 x} \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{5 x(2 x)-\left(x^2+25\right)(5)}{(5 x)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{x^2-25}{5 x^2} \\ & \text{ when } f^{\prime}(x)=0 \Rightarrow x^2-25=0 \Rightarrow x= \pm 5 \\ & \text{$ for $maximum value } x= \pm 5 \\ & \text{ when } \alpha=5 \\ & \sqrt{\alpha^2+2 \alpha-6}=\sqrt{25+10-6}=\sqrt{29} \\ & \text{ when } \alpha=-5 \\ & \sqrt{\alpha^2+2 \alpha-6}=\sqrt{25-10-6}=\sqrt{9}=3.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The equation of the normal at $t=\frac{\pi}{2}$ to the curve $\mathrm{x}=2 \sin t, y=2 \cos t$ is
questions.solution:
$x=2 \sin t, y=2 \cos t\therefore \quad x^2+y^2=4$

& \Rightarrow x²+4 x-x-4=0 \\
& x(x+4)-1(x+4)=0 \\

& x-1=0, x+4=0 \\
& x=1, x=-4
\end{aligned} Put in $ y^2=3 \mathrm{x}$, then, $y^2=3, y= \pm \sqrt{3}$. $(x, y) \rightarrow(1, \sqrt{3}) \ \text{ and } (1, \sqrt{3})$
Now, Differentiate both curves w.r.t $x \begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow x²+y²=4 \\
& 2 x+2 y $\cdot \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \\ \text{ and } y \frac{d y}{d x}=-$ x \\
& $\frac{d y}{d x}=-\frac{x}{y}$\\
& \Rightarrow y=$\sqrt{3 x}$\\
& $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2 \sqrt{x}}
\end{aligned}$ Put the point $(1, \sqrt{3})$ in their differentiation. $\begin{aligned}$& m_1=$\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}},$ m_2=$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$\\
& \tan $\theta=\left|\frac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1 m_2}\right|=\left|\frac{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\right|=\left|\frac{\frac{-2-3}{2 \sqrt{3}}}{\frac{1}{2}}\right|$\\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f \left(x\right) = \dfrac{6x^{2} - 18x + 21}{6x^{2} - 18x + 17}. If $ m$ is the maximum value of $f$\left(x\right)$ and $f\left(x\right) >$n ∀ x \in $\mathbb{R} Then 14m - 7n =$
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{6{x}^{2} - 18x + 21}{6{x}^{2} - 18x + 17}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = 1 + \dfrac{4}{6{x}^{2} - 18x + 17}$

Now let $g\left(x\right) = 6{x}^{2} - 18x + 17$

Now we will find minimum value of $g\left(x\right)$ by differentiating it we get,

${g}^{'}\left(x\right) = 12x - 18$

$⇒ {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0 ⇒ 12x - 18 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Now putting the value of $x$ in $g\left(x\right)$ we get, $g\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = \dfrac{7}{2}$

Now putting the minimum value of $g\left(x\right)$ in $f\left(x\right)$ we get,

$f{\left(x\right)}_{max} = 1 + \dfrac{8}{7} = \dfrac{15}{7}$

And minimum value of $f\left(x\right)$ will be tending to $1$, so $f\left(x\right) > 1$

Now on comparing with given data in question we get, $m = \dfrac{15}{7} \text{ and } n = 1$

So, $14m - 7n = 14 \times \dfrac{15}{7} - 7 = 30 - 7 = 23$

Volume of sphere, $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}$

i.e. $∆ V = 4\pir^{2} ∆ r$

$= 4\pi \times \left(10\right)^{2} \times \dfrac{0. 001}{4\pi} = 0. 1{cm}^{3}$

Point of intersection of& $y^{2} = 4x & x^{2} + y^{2} = 5:$

$x^{2} + 4x + 4 = 9 ⇒ x + 2 = \pm 3$

$⇒ x = 1, - 5 ( \text{rejected} ) & y = \pm 2$

Now, at~$\left(1, 2\right)$:

For~$y^{2} = 4x$

$⇒ {m}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\left(1, 2\right) = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1$

For~$x^{2} + y^{2} = 5$

$⇒ {m}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\left(1, 2\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now,~$tan\theta = \dfrac{{m}_{1} - {m}_{2}}{1 + {m}_{1}{m}_{2}}$

$= \dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}} = 3$

At~$\left(1, - 2\right)$

Hence,~$\left|tan\theta\right| = 3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the extreme value of $3x - 2x^{2} + 1$ is $k$ then the set of all real values of $x$ for which $kx^{2} + 2x + 1 > 0$& is
questions.solution:
Let $f\left(x\right) = 3x - 2x^{2} + 1$

Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 3 - 4x$

For extreme value,

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3 - 4x = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{3}{4}$

So,

$f\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = k$

$⇒ 3 \times \dfrac{3}{4} - 2 \times \dfrac{9}{16} + 1 = k$

$⇒ 36 - 18 + 16 = k$

$⇒ k = 34$

So, $34x^{2} + 2x + 1 > 0 ⋯ \left(i\right)$

But discriminant of $34x^{2} + 2x + 1$ is $D = 4 - 136 = - 132 < 0$

And, coefficient of $x^{2}$ is greater than zero, so& $\left(i\right)$ is true for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, hence required solution is $\left(- \infty , \infty\right)$.

questions.q: Consider two families of curves $y^{2} = 4ax$ ($a$ is a parameter) and $x^{2} + \dfrac{y2}{2} = c^{2}$ ($c$ is parameter). If one curve from each family is chosen, then the angle between those two curves is
questions.solution:
Given two families of curves ${y}^{2} = 4ax$ ($a$ is a parameter) and ${x}^{2} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{2} = {c}^{2}$ ($c$ is parameter).

So,

$\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{x} = 4a . . . . \left(1\right)$

Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get

$- \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{2y}{x}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = {m}_{1} = \dfrac{y}{2x}$

And,

$2{x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = {c}^{2} . . . . \left(2\right)$

Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get

$4x + 2y\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = {m}_{2} = - \dfrac{2x}{y}$

Here,

${m}_{1}{m}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{y}{2x}\right)\left(\dfrac{- 2x}{y}\right) = - 1$

Therefore, angle between the curves is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.q: If $y = \log_{2}(\sin x),$ then the minimum value of $coshy$ is
questions.solution:
We know that $coshy = \dfrac{{e}^{y} + {e}^{- y}}{2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Let $u = \dfrac{{e}^{y} + {e}^{- y}}{2},$ to find the maximum or minimum value of $u,$ find the points at which $\dfrac{du}{dy} = 0 .$

We have $u = \dfrac{{e}^{y} + {e}^{- y}}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{du}{dy} = \dfrac{{e}^{y} - {e}^{- y}}{2}$

Now $\dfrac{du}{dy} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{{e}^{y} - {e}^{- y}}{2} = 0$

$⇒ {e}^{y} - \dfrac{1}{{e}^{y}} = 0$

$⇒ {e}^{2y} = 1$

$⇒ 2y = 0$

$⇒ y = 0 .$

Now, $\dfrac{{d}^{2}u}{d{y}^{2}} = \dfrac{{e}^{y} + {e}^{- y}}{2} > 0$

We know that if the second derivative of a function is positive, then the function has a point of minima.

Hence, $u = coshy = \dfrac{{e}^{y} + {e}^{- y}}{2}$ is minimum at $y = 0$ and the minimum value is

$coshy = \dfrac{{e}^{0} + {e}^{0}}{2} = \dfrac{1 + 1}{2} = 1 .$

questions.q: If $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}x, & 0 \leq x \leq 1 \\ 2-x, & 1 \leq x \leq 2\end{array}, \quad\right.$ then Rolle's theorem is not applicable to $f(x)$ because
questions.solution:
We have,

$$\begin{aligned}& f(x)=\left\{$\begin{array}{cc}
x, & 0 \leq x \leq 1 \\
2-x, & 1 \leq x \leq 2
\end{array}$\right. \\
 \text{ LHL }=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{-}}$ x \\
& =$\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}(1-h)=1 \\
 \text{ RHL }=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{+}}(2-x)=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0^{+}}\{2-(1+h)\}=1 \\
 \text{$ and } \quad$ f(1)=2-1=1 \\
& \therefore \quad $\mathrm{LHL}=\mathrm{RHL}=  f(1) \\
&

Hence, $ f(x)$ is continuous.
Also, $f^{\prime}$\left(1^{-}\right)=1$$ and $f^{\prime}\left(1^{+}\right)=-1$

questions.solution:
Let A$ be the area and $xbe the side of $an equilateral triangle. \therefore A=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$ x^2 on differentiating both sides w.r.t. $ X$, we get $\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d A}{d x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(2 x) \\

questions.q: The height of the cone of maximum volume inscribed in a sphere of radius $R$ is
questions.solution:
Let the height of the cone $=h$ and the radius of the cone $=r$ Given, radius of the sphere $=R$ Now, In $\triangle O P B$
$\Rightarrow \quad R^2=r^2+(h-R)^2$ $\Rightarrow \quad r^2=R^2-(h-R)^2$ $=(R+h-R)(R-h+R)$ $\Rightarrow \quad r^2=h(2 R-h)$ The volume of the cone is $V=\frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h$ $\Rightarrow \quad V=\frac{1}{3} \pi h(2 R-h) h$ $\Rightarrow \quad V=\frac{\pi}{3}\left(2 R h^2-h^3\right)$ Differentiating with $r$ to $h$ $\frac{d V}{d h}=\frac{\pi}{3}\left(4 R h-3 h^2\right)$ For maximum or minimum value of volume $\frac{d V}{d h}=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\pi}{3}\left(4 R h-3 h^2\right)=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad h(4 R-3 h)=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad h=0, h=\frac{4 R}{3} \quad$ (Not possible) Now, $\quad \frac{d^2 V}{d h^2}=\frac{\pi}{3}(4 R-6 h)$ $\left(\frac{d^2 V}{d h^2}\right)_{\left(\text{at } h=\frac{4 R}{3}\right)}=\frac{\pi}{3}\left(4 R-6 \cdot \frac{4 R}{3}\right)$ $=\frac{\pi}{3}(4 R-8 R)=-\frac{4 \pi}{3} R \Rightarrow$ Negative ie., Maximum Hence, the height of the cone of maximum volume is $\left(\frac{4 R}{3}\right)$.

questions.solution:
Let $\quad y=\frac{\log x}{x}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x \cdot \frac{1}{x}-\log x}{x^2}=\frac{1-\log x}{x^2}$
Put $\quad \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow \log x=1\Rightarrow \quad x=e$

Hence, maximum value at $x=e$ is $\frac{1}{e}$.

length of normal

questions.q: The function $f(x)=x^3+a x^2+b x+c, a^2 \leq 3 b$ has
options: one maximum and one minimum value
one maximum and one minimum value
questions.solution:
Given, $f(x)=x^3+a x^2+b x+c, a^2 \leq 3 b$.
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\begin{aligned} & f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^2+2 a x+b \\ & \text{ Put } \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 3 x^2+2 a x+b=0 \\ & \end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad x & =\frac{-2 a \pm \sqrt{4 a^2-12 b}}{2 \times 3} \\
& =\frac{-2 a \pm 2 \sqrt{a^2-3 b}}{3}
\end{aligned}$
Since, $\quad a^2 \leq 3 b$, $\therefore \quad x$ has an imaginary value. Hence, no extreme value of $x$ exist.

questions.q: If $x$ is real, then the minimum value of $\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}$, is
questions.solution: On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get $f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{\left(x^2+x+1\right)(2 x-1)-\left(x^2-x+1\right)(2 x+1)}{\left(x^2+x+1\right)^2}$ for maximum or minimum, put $f^{\prime}(x)=0\begin{array}{lc} \Rightarrow & \left(x^2+x+1\right)(2 x-1)-\left(x^2-x+1\right)(2 x+1)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & x^2+x-1-\left(-x^2+x+1\right)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 x^2-2=0 \Rightarrow x= \pm 1 \end{array}$ Now, $f^{\prime}(c)=\frac{2 x^2-2}{\left(x^2+x+1\right)^2}$ Again differentiating, we get $\begin{aligned} & \left(x^2+x+1\right)^2(4 x)-\left(2 x^2-2\right) \\ & f^{\prime \prime}(x)=\frac{2\left(x^2+x+1\right)(2 x+1)}{\left(x^2+x+1\right)^4} \end{aligned}$ at $x=1, f^{\prime \prime}(x) > 0$ Therefore it is minimum at $x=1$ Put $x=1$ in equation (i), we get $f(1)=\frac{1-1+1}{1+1+1}=\frac{1}{3}\therefore$ The minimum value is $\frac{1}{3}$.

\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area enclosed by the curves $y=8 x-x^2$ and $8 x-4 y+11=0$ is
questions.solution:
Given equation of curves are $$ \begin{aligned} & y=8 x-x^2 \\ & 8 x-4 y+11=0 \end{aligned} $$ Eq. (i) can be rewritten as $$ \begin{aligned} & y=-\left(x^2-2 \cdot 4 x+4^2-4^2\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=-\left[(x-4)^2-16\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y-16=-(x-4)^2 \\ & \end{aligned} $$ $(x-4)^2=-(y-16)$, which represent a parabola open downward and having vertex at $(4,16)$. Clearly, Eq. (ii) represent a straight line passing through $\left(0, \frac{11}{4}\right)$ and $\left(-\frac{11}{8}, 0\right)$ Let us find the point of intersection of given curves, for this substitute the value of $y$ from Eq. (i) in Eq. (ii). $$ \begin{array}{rlrl} \Rightarrow & 8 x-4\left(8 x-x^2\right)+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow & 8 x-32 x+4 x^2+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow & 4 x^2-24 x+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow & 4 x^2-22 x-2 x+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 x(2 x-11)-1(2 x-11) =0 \\ \Rightarrow & (2 x-1)(2 x-11) =0 \\ \Rightarrow & x =\frac{1}{2} \text{ or } \frac{11}{2} \end{array} $$ When $x=\frac{1}{2}$, then $y=\frac{15}{4}$ When $x=\frac{11}{2}$, then $y=\frac{55}{4} \quad$ [using Eq. (ii)] Now, required area $=$ Area of shaded region.
$$ =\int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}[y(\text{ parabola })-y(\text{ straight line })] d x $$ $$ \begin{aligned} & =\int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}\left[8 x-x^2-\left(\frac{8 x+11}{4}\right)\right] d x \\ & =\frac{1}{4} \int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}\left(32 x-4 x^2-8 x-11\right) d x \\ & =-\frac{1}{4} \int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}\left(4 x^2-24 x+11\right) d x \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{4 x^3}{3}-24 \frac{x^2}{2}+11 x\right]_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left\{\left[\frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{1331}{8}-12 \times \frac{121}{4}+\frac{121}{2}\right]-\left[\frac{1}{6}-3+\frac{11}{2}\right]\right\} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left\{\frac{1331}{6}-363+\frac{121}{2}-\frac{1}{6}+3-\frac{11}{2}\right\} \\ & =\frac{-1}{4}\left\{\frac{1330}{6}-360+55\right\} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left\{\frac{665}{3}-305\right\} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left\{\frac{665-915}{3}\right\}=\frac{250}{4 \times 3}=\frac{125}{6} \text{ sq units } \end{aligned} $$

Given curves are

(i), Area of region $O A B C O=2 \times\left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)$ $=\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

Given that $y = {x}^{4} - {x}^{2}$

For minimum points of curve:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({x}^{4} - {x}^{2}\right) = 0$

$4{x}^{3} - 2x = 0$

$2x\left(2{x}^{2} - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2x = 0$ or $2{x}^{2} - 1 = 0$

$x = 0$ or $x = \dfrac{\pm 1}{\sqrt{2}}$

So $f$ is minimum at $\dfrac{\pm 1}{\sqrt{2}}$

The area $= \left|{∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left({x}^{4} - {x}^{2}\right)dx\right|$

$= \left|2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left({x}^{4} - {x}^{2}\right)dx\right|\left[∵ f\left(x\right)\text{is even function}\right]$

$= \left|2\left[\dfrac{{x}^{5}}{5} - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right]\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} 0\right|$

$= \left|2\left({\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{5} - {\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|$

$= \left|2\left(\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{3 - 10}{30\sqrt{2}}\right|$

$∴$ Area $= \dfrac{7}{30\sqrt{2}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For any $n \in \mathbb{N}, 4^n+15 n-1$ is divisible by
questions.solution:
Let $P(n): 4^n+15 n-1$ is divisible by 9 .
For $n=1, P(1)=4^1+15 \times 1-1=18$, which is divisible by 9 .
$\therefore P(1)$ is true.
Let $P(k)$ be true. Then, $4^k+15 k-1$ is divisible by 9 .
$\Rightarrow 4^k+15 k-1=9 \lambda$, for some $\lambda \in N$.
We shall now show that $P(k+1)$ is true. For this, we have to show that $4^{k+1}+15(k+1)-1$ is divisible by 9 .
Now, $4^{k+1}+15(k+1)-1=4^k \cdot 4+15(k+1)-1 \begin{aligned}& =(9 \lambda-15 k+1) \times4+15(k+1)-1 \\
& =36 \lambda-45 k+18 \\
& =9(4 \lambda-5 k+2), \text{ which is divisible by }9 .
\end{aligned} $\therefore P(k+1)$ is true.
Thus, $P(k)$ is true $\Rightarrow P(k+1)$ is true. Hence, by PMI, $P(n)$ is true for all $n \in N$.$

questions.q: In the binomial expansion of $( 1 + x{)}^{2k},$ if its middle term is the only numerically greatest term, then $x$ lies in the interval
questions.solution:
The middle term in the& binomial expansion of& $\left(1 + x\right)n,$~when& $n$~is even is& ${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n x^{r},$~where& $r = \dfrac{n}{2} .

The middle term$ in the binomial expansion of~$\left(1 + x\right)$2k$~is& ${T}_{k + 1} = Ck 2k \times x^{k} .

Given,$ the middle term is the only greatest term, hence

\left|\dfrac{Tk + 1}{Tk}\right| > 1$~and& $\left|\dfrac{Tk + 1}{Tk + 2}\right| > 1$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{Ck 2k \times x^{k}}{Ck - 1 2k \times x\left(k - 1\right)}\right| > 1$~and& $\left|\dfrac{Ck 2k \times x^{k}}{Ck + 1 2k \times x\left(k + 1\right)}\right| > 1$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{\dfrac{\left(2k\right) !}{k ! \times k !} \times x}{\dfrac{\left(2k\right) !}{\left(k - 1\right) ! \times \left(k + 1\right) !}}\right| > 1$~and& $\left|\dfrac{\dfrac{\left(2k\right) !}{k ! \times k !}}{\dfrac{\left(2k\right) !}{\left(k + 1\right) ! \times \left(k - 1\right) !} \times x}\right| > 1$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{\left(k - 1\right) ! \times \left(k + 1\right) !}{k ! \times k !} \times x\right| > 1$~and& $\left|\dfrac{\left(k + 1\right) ! \times \left(k - 1\right) !}{k ! \times k ! \times x}\right| > 1$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{\left(k - 1\right) ! \times \left(k + 1\right) \times k !}{k \times \left(k - 1\right) ! \times k !} \times x\right| > 1$~and& $\left|\dfrac{\left(k + 1\right) \times k ! \times \left(k - 1\right) !}{k ! \times k \times \left(k - 1\right) ! \times x}\right| > 1$

$⇒ \left|\left(k + 1\right)k \times x\right| > 1$~and& $\left|\dfrac{k + 1}{k \times x}\right| > 1$

$⇒ \left|x\right| > \dfrac{k}{k + 1}$~and& $\left|x\right| < \dfrac{k + 1}{k} .

Both$ of which imply~$\left|x\right|$ < $\dfrac{k + 1}{k}$ .

We know that, the solution of~$\left|x\right| < a$~is& - a < x < a .

Thus, the $solution of~\left|x\right| < \dfrac{k + 1}{k}~is&$- $\dfrac{k + 1}{k} < x < \dfrac{k + 1}{k}$ .

questions.q: For $x > 0,$~if $p^{th }$term is the first negative term in the expansion of $\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{5}\right)22 / 3$and in the~expansion of $\left(1 - \dfrac{3x}{5}\right)22 / 3$ from $r^{th}$term onwards all the terms are positive, then the~number of terms in the expansion of $\left(px + \dfrac{r}{x}\right)pr$ is
questions.solution:
For negative/rational index $n$,

${\left(1 + x\right)}^{n} = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)}{2 !} + . . . . . + \dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right)\left(n - 3\right) . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(n - r + 1\right)}{r !}{x}^{r} + . . . .$

In the given expansion ${\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{5}\right)}^{22 / 3}$, ${p}^{th}$ term is first negative term.

$∴ {T}_{p} = \dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right)\left(n - 3\right) . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(n - p + 2\right)}{\left(p - 1\right) !}{x}^{p - 1}\left[\text{Here}, n = \dfrac{22}{3}\right]$

Here, $n - p + 2 < 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{22}{3} - p + 2 < 0$

$⇒ - p < - \dfrac{28}{3}$

$⇒ p > 9 . 33$

$∴ p = 10$

Also in the expansion of ${\left(1 - \dfrac{3x}{5}\right)}^{22 / 3}$ from ${r}^{th}$ term onwards all terms are positive.

$∴ {T}_{r} = {\left(- 1\right)}^{r - 1}\dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right)\left(n - 3\right) . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(n - r + 2\right)}{\left(r - 1\right) !}{x}^{r - 1}\left[\text{Here}, n = \dfrac{22}{3}\right]$

$∴ n - r + 2 < 0 \text{ and } r - 1$ is odd.

$⇒ \dfrac{22}{3} - r + 2 < 0$

$⇒ r > 9 . 33$

$∴ r = 10$ 

Now, In the expansion ${\left(px + \dfrac{r}{x}\right)}^{pr}\text{i.e.}$ ${\left(10x + \dfrac{10}{x}\right)}^{100}$,

So, number of terms$= 100 + 1 = 101$.

questions.q:
Sum of the coefficients of $x^{r}, ( r = 0, 1, 2, 3, . . . , 15 )$ in the expansion of $( 3x - 1{)}^{15}$ is equal to the sum of the binomial coefficients of which of the following expansions?

$\left(a\right)$~$( 1 + x{)}^{15}$

$\left(b\right)$~$( 1 + x{)}^{16} + ( 1 - x{)}^{16}$

$\left(c\right)$~$( 1 + x{)}^{16} - ( 1 - x{)}^{16}$
questions.solution:
The binomial expansion of ${\left(a + b\right)}^{n} = C0 n {a}^{n}{b}^{0} + C1 n {a}^{n - 1}{b}^{1} + C2 n {a}^{n - 2}{b}^{2} + . . . + Cn n {a}^{0}{b}^{n}$ and to find the sum of coefficients of all the powers of $x,$ put $x = 1,$ in the expansion.

Hence, the sum of coefficients of all the powers of $x,$ in ${\left(3x - 1\right)}^{15}$

is ${\left(3 \times 1 - 1\right)}^{15} = {2}^{15} .

Also, the sum$ of coefficients of all the powers of x,$ in ${$\left(1 + x\right)$}^{15}$ is ${$\left(1 + 1\right)$}^{15} = {2}^{15} .

Also, the sum$ of coefficients of all the powers of x,$ in ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{16}$ is ${\left(1 + 1\right)}^{16} = {2}^{16}$ and in ${\left(1 - x\right)}^{16}$ is ${\left(1 - 1\right)}^{16} = 0 .

We know that ${$\left(a + b\right)$}^{n} + {$\left(a - b\right)$}^{n} = 2 $\left[C0 n {a}^{n}{b}^{0} + C2 n {a}^{n - 2}{b}^{2} + C4 n {a}^{n - 4}{b}^{4} + . . .\right]$ and

${\left(a + b\right)$}^{n} - {$\left(a - b\right)}^{n} = 2\left[C1 n {a}^{n - 1}b + C3 n {a}^{n - 3}{b}^{3} + C5 n {a}^{n - 5}{b}^{5} + . . .\right] .

Hence, ${$\left(1 + x\right)}^{16} + {\left(1 - x\right)}^{16} = 2 \left[C0 16 + C2 16 {x}^{2} + C4 16 {x}^{4} + . . . + C16 16 {x}^{16}\right] and

${$\left(1 + x\right)$}^{16} - {$\left(1 - x\right)$}^{16} = 2 $\left[C1 16 x + C3 16 {x}^{3} + C5 16 {x}^{5} + . . . + C15 16 {x}^{15}\right]$ .

But $r = 0, 1, 2, . . . , 15,$ hence the sum of coefficients of all the powers of $x,$ in ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{16} + {\left(1 - x\right)}^{16}$ is $\dfrac{{2}^{16} + 0}{2} - C16 16 = {2}^{15} - 1$ and in ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{16} - {\left(1 - x\right)}^{16}$ is $\dfrac{{2}^{16} - 0}{2} = {2}^{15} .

Hence,$ the sum of coefficients of {x}^{r}, $\left(r = 0, 1, 2, . . . , 15\right)$ in the expansion of ${\left(3x - 1\right)}^{15}$ is same as the sum of the binomial coefficients of ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{15}$ and ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{16} - {\left(1 - x\right)}^{16}$ i.e. $\left(a\right)$ and $\left(c\right)$ only.

questions.q: For $|x| < \frac{1}{2}$, if the coefficient of $x^{10}$ and the constant term in the expansion of $\frac{2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x-2}{(1-x)(1+x)(1-2 x)}$ in powers of $x$ are $l$ and $m$ respectively, then $1 m=$
questions.solution:
The given expression is
$\frac{2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x-2}{(1-x)(1+x)(1-2 x)}=\frac{2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x-2}{(2 x-1)(x-1)(x+1)}=1+\frac{A}{2 x-1}+\frac{B}{x-1}+\frac{C}{x+1}$
(By partial fraction)
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow 2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x & -2 \\ =\left(2 x^3\right. & \left.-x^2-2 x+1\right)+A\left(x^2-1\right) \\ & +B\left(2 x^2+x-1\right)+C\left(2 x^2-3 x+1\right)\end{aligned}$
On comparing, we get
$\begin{aligned}-1+A+2 B+2 C & =8 \\ -2+B-3 C & =-2\end{aligned}$ and $\quad 1-A-B+C=-2$
On solving we have A=1, B=3 and $C=1\therefore$ Given expression is
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x-2}{(1-x)(1+x)(1-2 x)}=1-\frac{1}{1-2 x}-\frac{3}{1-x}+\frac{1}{1+x} \\ = & 1-(1-2 x)^{-1}-3(1-x)^{-1}+(1+x)^{-1}\end{aligned}\therefore$ Coefficient of $x^{10}$ is
$-2^{10}-3+1=-2-2^{10}=l$
and constant term is $1-1-3+1=-2=m\therefore \quad l m=4  \left(1+2^9\right)$

questions.q: $n^5-5 n^3+4 n$ is divisible by 120 is true for
questions.solution:
Since, $n^5-5 n^3+4 n=n\left(n^4-5 n^2+4\right)=n\left(n^4-4 n^2-n^2+4\right)=n\left(n^2-1\right)\left(n^2-4\right)=(n-2)(n-1)(n)(n+1)(n+2)=P(n)$ (let)
For $n=1,2, P(n)$ is zero so it is divisible by 120. and for $n=3, P(3)=5 !=120$ and so on, so the $P(n)$ is divisible by 120 for all positive integers $n$.

In the expansion of $(1+x)^{15}$ the coefficient of x^{10}=\binom{15}{10} $\text{. }$ And the expansion of (1-x)^{-n}=1+n x+$\frac{n(n+1)}{2 !}$ x^2+$\frac{n(n+1)(n+2) x^3}{3 !}+\ldots$ So, coefficient of $x^5=\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)}{5 !}$
According to the question, $\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)}{5 !}=\binom{15}{10} \begin{gathered}

\Rightarrow $\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)}{5 !}=7 \times13 \times3 \times11 \\

\Rightarrow n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)=11 \times12 \times13 \times14 \times15
\end{gathered} By comparing, we get n=11
$

questions.solution:
In the expansion of $\left(ax^{2} + \dfrac{1}{bx}\right)13$

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 13 \left(ax^{2}\right)13 - r\left(\dfrac{1}{bx}\right)r = Cr 13 \dfrac{a13 - r}{br}x^{26 - 3r}$

Here, $26 - 3r = 5$

$⇒ 26 - 5 = 3r$

$⇒ 3r = 21 ⇒ r = 7$

Coefficient of term containing $x^{5}$ is $C7 13 \dfrac{a13 - 7}{b7} = C7 13 \dfrac{a6}{b7}$.

In the expansion of $\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{bx^{2}}\right)13$

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 13 \left(ax\right)13 - r\left(\dfrac{- 1}{bx^{2}}\right)r = \left(- 1\right)r \times Cr 13 \dfrac{a13 - r}{br}x^{13 - 3r}$

$⇒ 13 - 3r = - 5$

$⇒ 13 + 5 = 3r ⇒ r = \dfrac{18}{3} ⇒ r = 6$

The coefficient of term containing $x^{- 5}$ is $\left(- 1\right)6$.

$⇒ C6 13 \dfrac{a13 - 6}{b6} = C6 13 \dfrac{a7}{b6}$

$⇒ C7 13 \dfrac{a6}{b7} = C6 13 \dfrac{a7}{b6}$

$⇒ \dfrac{a6}{b7} = \dfrac{a7}{b6}$

$⇒ \dfrac{a^{7}b^{7}}{a^{6}b^{6}} = 1$

$∴ ab = 1$

questions.q: The remainder when $7^n-6 n-50(n \in \mathbb{N})$ is divided by 36 , is
questions.solution:
We have, $7^n=(1+6)^n \begin{aligned}& ={ }^n C_0+{ }^n C_1 6{ }^1+{ }^n C_2 6^2+{ }^n C_3 6^3+\ldots+{ }^n C_n 6^n \\
& =1+6 n+66^2\left[{ }^n C_2+{ }^n C_3 6+\ldots+{ }^n C_n 66^{n-2}\right] \\
& =1+6 n+36 \lambda \quad\left[\text{ where, }{ }^n C_2+\ldots+{ }^n C_n 6^{n-2}=\lambda\right] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 7^n-6 n=36 \lambda+1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 7^n-6 n-50=36 \lambda-49 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 7^n-6 n-50=36 \lambda-72+23 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 7^n-6 n-50=36(\lambda-2)+23
\end{aligned}

\Rightarrow \quad 7^n-6 n-50=36 \mu+23[\text{ where } \lambda-2=\mu]

$\therefore$ When 7^n-6 n-50$ is divided by 36 , then remainder will be equal to 23 .

& =\frac{3 n}{2} \cdot{ }^{2 n} C_n-{ }^{2 n} C_n={ }^{2 n} C_n\left(\frac{3 n}{2}-1\right) \\

We know that

${\left(1 + x\right)}^{n} = 1 + \dfrac{n}{1}x + \dfrac{n ( n - 1 )}{2}{x}^{2} + . . . . . . . .$

Where $x = \left(\dfrac{- 3}{4}x\right)$ and $n = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$, then

$\dfrac{1}{2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{3x}{4}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{- 3}{4}x\right)}{1}\right] + \dfrac{\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 1\right)}{2}{\left(\dfrac{- 3}{4}x\right)}^{2} + . . . . .$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{3x}{4}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[1 + \dfrac{3}{8}x + \dfrac{\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\left(- \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\right)}{2}\left(\dfrac{9}{16}{x}^{2}\right) + . . . . .\right]$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{3x}{4}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[1 + \dfrac{3}{8}x + \dfrac{27}{128}{x}^{2} + . . . . . . .\right]$

Hence, approximate value is 

$= \left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{16}x + \dfrac{27}{256}{x}^{2}\right)$

questions.solution:

Then by binomial expansion 
$={ }^{10} C_0+{ }^{10} C_1 x(2+3 x)+{ }^{10} C_2 x^2(2+3 x)^2+\ldots$

$=3 \cdot{ }^{10} C_1+4 \cdot{ }^{10} C_2$
ie., $a_2=3 \cdot 10+4 \cdot 45=30+180=210$
So, $\quad \frac{a_2}{a_1}=\frac{210}{20}=10.5$

&

questions.q: If $x$ and $y$ are two positive real numbers such that $x+i y=\frac{13 \sqrt{-5+12 i}}{(2-3 i)(3+2 i)}$ then $13 y-26 x=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ (a) } x+i y=\frac{13 \sqrt{-5+12}}{(2-3 i)(3+2 i)} \\
& =\frac{13(2+3 i)(3-2 i)}{13 \times 13} \sqrt{-5+12 i}....(i) \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{-5+12 i}= \pm(a+i b)
\end{aligned}$
(Using square root of complex number)
$\begin{aligned}
& a^2=\frac{\sqrt{5^2+12^2}-5}{2}, b^2=\frac{\sqrt{5^2+12^2}-(-5)}{2} \\
& a= \pm 2, b= \pm 3 \\
& \therefore \sqrt{-5+12 i}= \pm(2+3 i)...(ii) \\
& =+(2+3 i) \quad \text{ (as } x \text{ and } y \text{ are positive })
\end{aligned}$
From (i) and (ii),
$\begin{aligned}
& x+i y=\frac{(2+3 i)(3-2 i)(2+3 i)}{13}=\frac{9+46 i}{13} \\
& \Rightarrow x=\frac{9}{13}, y=\frac{46}{13} \Rightarrow 13 y-26 x=46-18=28
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & Z_1=\sqrt{3}+i \sqrt{3} \\ & r_1= \sqrt{6}, \theta_1=\tan ^{-1} 1=\frac{\pi}{4} \Rightarrow Z_1=\sqrt{6} e^{i \frac{\pi}{4}} \\ & Z_2=\sqrt{3}+i, r^2=2, \theta_2=\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\pi}{6} \\ & \Rightarrow Z_2=2 e^{i \frac{\pi}{6}}\end{aligned}$
Now, $\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}=\frac{\sqrt{6} e^{i \frac{\pi}{4}}}{2 e^{i \frac{\pi}{4}}}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} e^{i \frac{\pi}{12}}$ And $\left(\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}\right)^{50}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\right)^{50} e^{i \frac{50 \pi}{12}}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\right)^{50} e^{i\left(4 \pi+\frac{2 \pi}{12}\right)}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\right)^{50} e^{i \frac{\pi}{6}}$

questions.solution: $\sqrt{5}-i \sqrt{15}=2 \sqrt{5}\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{i \sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\begin{aligned} & \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \sec \theta=2 \\ & \sin \theta=\frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2} \Rightarrow \operatorname{cosec} \theta=\frac{-2}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & r=2 \sqrt{5} \\ & r^2\left(\sec \theta+3 \operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta\right)=20 \times\left(2+3 \times \frac{4}{3}\right)=120.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: One of the roots of the equation $x^{14}+x^9-x^5-1=0$ is
questions.solution: $x^{14}+x^9-x^5-1=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left(x^9-1\right)\left(x^5+1\right)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^5=-1 \text{$ or $} x^9=1 \\ & \Rightarrow x^5=\cos 180^{{}^{\circ}}+i \sin 180^{{}^{\circ}} \\ & \Rightarrow x=\cos \left(\frac{180}{5}\right)+i \sin \left(\frac{180}{5}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow x=\cos 36^{{}^{\circ}}+i \sin 36^{{}^{\circ}} \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}+\frac{i \sqrt{10-2 \sqrt{5}}}{4}.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $x=a+b, y=a \alpha+b \beta, z=a \beta+b \alpha$ and $\alpha, \beta$ are the complex cube roots of unity, then $x^3+y^3+z^3=$
questions.solution: $x=a+b\begin{aligned} & y=a \alpha+b \beta, z=a \beta+b \alpha \\ & \alpha=\omega \text{ and } \beta=\omega^2 \\ & \because x+y+z=(a+a \alpha+a \beta)+(b+b \beta+b \alpha) \\ & =a(1+\alpha+\beta)+b(1+\beta+\alpha) \\ & =a\left(1+\omega+\omega^2\right)+b\left(1+\omega+\omega^2\right)=0 \\ & \therefore x^3+y^3+z^3=3 x y z \\ & =3(a+b)\left(a \omega+b \omega^2\right)\left(a \omega^2+b \omega\right)\end{aligned}$$\begin{array}{r}=3\left(a^3 \omega^3+a^2 b \omega^2+a^2 b \omega^4+a b^2 \omega^3+b a^2 \omega^3+b^2 a \omega^2+\right. \\ a b^2 \omega^2+b^3 \omega^3\end{array} \begin{aligned}$& =3$\left($a^3+b³+a² b $\omega^$2+a² b $\omega+$a b²+a² b+a b² $\omega^$2+a b² $\omega^$2\right) \\ & =3$\left[$a^3+b³+a b²$\left($1+$\omega+\omega^$2\right)+a² b$\left(\omega^$2+$\omega+$1\right)\right] \\ & =3$\left($a^3+b³\right)\end{aligned}

questions.q: If $z=x+i y$ is a complex number such that $z \bar{z}+\bar{z} z^3=350$ and $x, y$ are integers, then $|z|=$
questions.solution: $\mathrm{Z} \overline{\mathrm{Z}^3+\overline{\mathrm{Z}} \mathrm{Z}^3=350\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{Z} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{Z}}\left(\overline{\mathrm{Z}^2+\mathrm{Z}^2\right)=350 \\ & |\mathrm{Z}|^2\left((x-i y)^2+(x+i y)^2\right)=350 \\ & |\mathrm{Z}|^2\left(x^2-y^2-2 x y i+x^2-y^2+2 x y i\right)=350 \\ & 2 \cdot|\mathrm{Z}|^2\left(x^2-y^2\right)=350 \\ & |\mathrm{Z}|^2\left(x^2-y^2\right)=175=25 \times 7 \\ & \therefore|\mathrm{Z}|^2=25 \Rightarrow|\mathrm{Z}|=5\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta$ are the roots of the equation $x^2+x+1=0$, then $(\alpha+\beta)^2+\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2\right)^2+\left(\alpha^3+\beta^3\right)^2+\ldots+\left(\alpha^{12}+\beta^{12}\right)^2=$
questions.solution:
Since, roots of equation $x^2+x+1=0$ are complex cube roots of unity
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore(\alpha+\beta)^2+\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2\right)^2+\ldots \ldots . .+\left(\alpha^{12}+\beta^{12}\right)^2 \\ & =\left(\omega+\omega^2\right)^2+\left(\omega^2+\omega^4\right)^2+\ldots \ldots . .+\left(\omega^{12}+\omega^{24}\right)^2 \\ & \because 1+\omega+\omega^2=0 \text{ and } \omega^3=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \omega^n+\left(\omega^2\right)^n=2, n \text{ is multiple cf } 3 \\ & \omega^n+\left(\omega^2\right)^n=-1, n \text{ is not multiple of } 3 \\ & \therefore\left[(-1)^2+(-1)^2+(2)^2\right]+\ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots . .4 \text{ times } \\ & =6 \times 4=24\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The least positive integral value of $n$ such that $\left[\frac{1+\sin \frac{2 \pi}{9}+i \cos \frac{2 \pi}{9}}{1+\sin \frac{2 \pi}{9}-i \cos \frac{2 \pi}{9}}\right]^n=1$ is
questions.solution: $\left[\frac{1+\sin \frac{2 \pi}{9}+i \cos \frac{2 \pi}{9}}{1+\sin \frac{2 \pi}{9}-i \cos \frac{2 \pi}{9}}\right]^n=1\Rightarrow \frac{\left[\frac{1+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{2 \pi}{9}\right)+i \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{2 \pi}{9}\right)}{1+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{2 \pi}{9}\right)-i \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{2 \pi}{9}\right)}\right]^n}{n}=1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left[\frac{1+\cos \frac{5 \pi}{18}+i \sin \frac{5 \pi}{18}}{1+\cos \frac{5 \pi}{18}-i \sin \frac{5 \pi}{18}}\right]=1 \\ & \Rightarrow\left[\frac{2 \cos ^2 \frac{5 \pi}{36}+i 2 \sin \frac{5 \pi}{36} \cos \frac{5 \pi}{36}}{2 \cos ^2 \frac{5 \pi}{36}-i 2 \sin \frac{5 \pi}{36} \cos \frac{5 \pi}{36}}\right]^n=1 \\ & \Rightarrow\left[\frac{\cos \frac{5 \pi}{36}+i \sin \frac{5 \pi}{36}}{\cos \frac{5 \pi}{36}-i \sin \frac{5 \pi}{36}}\right)^n=1 \Rightarrow\left(\frac{e^{i 5 \pi / 36}}{e^{-i 5 \pi / 36}}\right)^n=1 \\ & \Rightarrow e^{i 5 n \pi / 18}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{5 n \pi}{18}=2 \mathrm{~K} \pi, \mathrm{K} \in \mathrm{I} \Rightarrow n=\frac{36 \mathrm{~K}}{5}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $i=\sqrt{-1}$ then $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{i}{3}\right)^n=$

questions.q: If $\mathrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}$ then $\operatorname{Arg}\left[\frac{(1+\mathrm{i})^{2025}}{(1-\mathrm{i})^{2022}}\right]=$
questions.solution: $\arg \left[\frac{(1+i)^{2025}}{(1-i)^{2022}}\right]\frac{(1+i)^{2025}}{(1-i)^{2022}}=\frac{(\sqrt{2})^{2025}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2025}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2022}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2022}}\begin{aligned} & =(\sqrt{2})^3 \frac{\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2025}}{\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2022}} \\ & =\sqrt{2} e^{i\left(\frac{2025 \pi}{4}+\frac{2022 \pi}{4}\right)}=\sqrt{2} e^{i\left(\frac{-\pi}{4}\right)} \\ & \therefore \arg (Z)=-\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $x_n=\cos \frac{\pi}{2^n}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{2^n}$, then $\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} x_n=$
questions.solution: $x_n=\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{2^n}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{2^n}\right)\begin{aligned} & =(\cos \pi+i \sin \pi)^{\frac{1}{2} n} \\ & \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} x_n=(\cos \pi+i \sin \pi)^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot(\cos \pi+i \sin \pi)^{\frac{1}{2^2}} \ldots \infty \\ & =(\cos \pi+i \sin \pi)^{\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{1-\frac{1}{2}}} \\ & =(\cos \pi+i \sin \pi)^1=-1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The locus of $z$ such that $\left|\frac{z-i}{z+i}\right|=2$, where $z=x+i y$, is
questions.solution: $\left|\frac{z-i}{z+i}\right|=2\begin{aligned} & \left|\frac{z-i}{z+i}\right|^2=2^2 \\ & \left(\frac{z-i}{z+i}\right) \overline{\left(\frac{z-i}{z+i}\right)}=2^2 \Rightarrow \frac{z-\bar{z}+z i-\bar{z} i+1}{z \bar{z}-i z+i \bar{z}+1}=4 \\ & z=x+\mathrm{i} y \\ & \frac{x^2+y^2+1+i(2 y i)}{x^2+y^2+1-i(2 y i)}=4 \\ & 3 x^2+3 y^2+10 y+3=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $z=x+i y$ and the point $P$ represents $z$ in the Argand plane. If the amplitude of $\left(\frac{2 z-i}{z+2 i}\right)$ is $\frac{\pi}{4}$, then the equation of the locus of P is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & z=x+i y \\ & \begin{array}{l}\left(\frac{2 z-i}{z+2 i}\right)=\frac{2 x+2 i y-i}{x+i y+2 i}=\frac{2 x+i(2 y-1)}{x+(y+2) i} \\ =\frac{(2 x+i(2 y-1))(x-(y+2) i)}{x^2+(y+2)^2} \\ =\frac{2 x^2+(2 y-1)(y+2)+i((2 y-1) x-2 x(y+2))}{x^2+(y+2)^2} \\ =\frac{\left(2 x^2+2 y^2+3 y-2\right)-5 i x}{x^2+(y+2)^2} \\ \operatorname{Arg}\left(\frac{2 z-i}{z+2 i}\right)=1 \Rightarrow \frac{-5 x}{2 x^2+2 y^2+3 y-2}=1 \\ \Rightarrow 2 x^2+2 y^2+3 y+5 x-2=0\end{array}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the roots of the equation $z^2-i=0$ are $\alpha$ and $\beta$, then $|\operatorname{Arg} \beta-\operatorname{Arg} \alpha|=$
questions.solution: $z^2-i=0\begin{aligned} & z^2=i=\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{2}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\ & z= \pm\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{2}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}= \pm\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ & =\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right),\left(-\cos \frac{\pi}{4}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ & =e^{i \frac{\pi}{4}}, e^{i \frac{5 \pi}{4}} \\ & \arg \beta=\frac{5 \pi}{4}, \arg \alpha=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & |\arg \beta-\arg \alpha|=\left|\frac{5 \pi}{4}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right|=\pi\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+i}{\sqrt{3}-i}\right)^4+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}-i}{\sqrt{3}+i}\right)^4=r$ cis $\theta$, then one of the values of $\sqrt{\mathrm{r} \operatorname{cis} \theta}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+i}{\sqrt{3}-i}\right)^4+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}-i}{\sqrt{3}+i}\right)^4\\ & =\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+i}{\sqrt{3}-i} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}+i}{\sqrt{3}+i}\right)^4+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}-i}{\sqrt{3}+i} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}-i}{\sqrt{3}-i}\right)^4\\ & =\left(\frac{(\sqrt{3}+i)^2}{4}\right)^4+\left(\frac{(\sqrt{3}-i)^2}{4}\right)^4\\ & =\frac{1}{4^4}\left[(\ssqrt{3}+i)^8+(\sqrt{3}- i)^8\right] \\ & =\frac{2^8}{4^4}\left[ \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{i}{2}\right)^8+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{i}{2}\right)^8\right]\\ & =\left[\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{6}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{6}\right)^8+ \left(\cos \frac{\pi}{6}- i \sin \frac{\pi}{6}\right)^8\right]\\ & =\left[\l lleft(e^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\right)^8+\lleft(e^{\left.\left.-i \frac{\pi}{6}\right)^8\rright]}=\left[e^{i 4 \pi/ 3}+e^{-i 4 \pi/ 3}\right]\right.\right. \\ & =e^{-i \frac{\pi}{3}+ e^{i \frac{\pi}{3}}=\cos \frac{\pi}{3}- i \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{3}+\cos \frac{\pi}{3}+ i \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{3}} \\ & =2 \cos \frac{\pi}{3}=1=r \operatorname{cis} \theta\end{aligned}\therefore \quad \sqrt{r \operatorname{cis} \theta}=\sqrt{1}=\operatorname{cis} \left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right).$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text Z=(\sqrt{3}-i)^{2 / 5} \\ & \Rightarrow Z=2^{\frac{1}{5}}(1-\sqrt{3} i)^{\frac{1}{5}} \\ & =2^{\frac{2}{5}}\left(\cos \left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+i \sin \left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)^{\frac{1}{5}} \\ & =2^{\frac{2}{5}}\left[\cos \frac{5 \pi}{3}+i \sin \frac{5 \pi}{3}\right]^{\frac{1}{5}}=2^{\frac{2}{5}}\left[\cos \frac{\pi}{3}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\right] \\ & =2^{\frac{2}{5}}\left[\frac{1}{2}+i \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right]=2^{-\frac{3}{5}}[1+i \sqrt{3}]\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\mathrm{z}=\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{iy}$ and the point $\mathrm{P}$ in the Argand plane represents $z$, then the locus of $z$ satisfying the equation $|z-2|+|z-2 i|=4$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text z=x+i y \\ & |z-2|+|z-2 i|=4 \\ & |(x-2)+i y|+|x+(y-2) i|=4 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{(x-2)^2+y^2}+\sqrt{x^2+(y-2)^2}=4 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad(x-2)^2+y^2=\left[4-\sqrt{x^2+(y-2)^2}\right]^2 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2+y^2-4 x+4 \\ & \quad=16+x^2+y^2+4-4 y-8 \sqrt{x^2+(y-2)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 4 y-4 x-16=-8 \sqrt{x^2+(y-2)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad(y-x-4)^2=4\left(x^2+(y-2)^2\right) \\ & \Rightarrow y^2+x^2+16-2 x y+8 x-8 y \\ & =4 x^2+4 y^2+16-16 y \\ & \Rightarrow 3 x^2+3 y^2+2 x y-8 x-8 y=0.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $i^{\prime} i^{\prime}$ is the root of the equation $\mathrm{x}^2+1=0$ then $(1+\sqrt{3} i)^{2023}+(1-\sqrt{3} i)^{2023}=$
questions.solution: $\Rightarrow(1+\sqrt{3} i)^{2023}+(1-\sqrt{3} i)^{2023}\begin{aligned} & =2^{2023}\left[\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} i\right)^{2023}+\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} i\right)^{2023}\right] \\ & =2^{2023}\left[\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{3}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\right)^{2023}+\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{3}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\right)^{2023}\right] \\ & =2^{2023}\left[\left(e^{i \pi / 3}\right)^{2023}+\left(e^{-i \pi / 3}\right)^{2023}\right] \\ & =2^{2023}\left[e^{i 2023 \frac{\pi}{3}}+e^{-i 2023 \frac{\pi}{3}}\right]=2^{2023}\left[e^{i \frac{\pi}{3}}+e^{-i \frac{\pi}{3}}\right] \\ & =2^{2023}\left[\cos \frac{\pi}{3}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{3}+\cos \frac{\pi}{3}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\right] \\ & =2^{2023} \times 2 \cos \frac{\pi}{3}=2^{2023}.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $z=1-\sqrt{3} i$, then $z^3-3 z^2+3 z=$
questions.solution:
Given, $z=1-\sqrt{3} i\begin{aligned} & z^2=1+3 i^2-2 \sqrt{3} i=-2(1+\sqrt{3} i) \\ & z^3=-2(1+\sqrt{3} i)(1-\sqrt{3} i)=-8 \end{aligned}$
Now, $z^3-3 z^2+3 z=-8+6+6 \sqrt{3} i+3-3 \sqrt{3} i=1+3 \sqrt{3} i$.

questions.q: $\operatorname{Arg}\left(\sin \frac{6 \pi}{5}+i\left(1+\cos \frac{6 \pi}{5}\right)\right)=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{Arg}\left(\sin \frac{6 \pi}{5}+i\left(1+\cos \frac{6 \pi}{5}\right)\right) \\ = & \operatorname{Arg}\left(2 \sin \frac{3 \pi}{5} \cdot \cos \frac{3 \pi}{5}+i \cdot 2 \cos ^2 \frac{3 \pi}{5}\right) \\ = & \operatorname{Arg}\left[\left(2 \cos \frac{3 \pi}{5}\right)\left(\sin \frac{3 \pi}{5}+i \cos \frac{3 \pi}{5}\right)\right] \\ = & \operatorname{Arg}\left[\left(2 \cos \frac{3 \pi}{5}\right)\left(\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{10}\right)+i \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{10}\right)\right)\right] \\ = & \operatorname{Arg}\left[\left(2 \cos \frac{3 \pi}{5}\right)\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{10}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{10}\right)\right] \\ \therefore & \quad \operatorname{Arg}\left(Z_1 \cdot Z_2\right)=\arg Z_1+\arg Z_2\end{aligned}=0-\frac{\pi}{10}=\frac{-\pi}{10}$ or $\pi-\frac{\pi}{10}=\frac{9 \pi}{10}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{iy}=\sqrt{\frac{3+i}{1+3 i}}$, then $\left(x^2+y^2\right)^2=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & x+i y=\sqrt{\frac{3+i}{1+3 i}}=\sqrt{\frac{(3+i)}{(1+3 i)} \times \frac{(1-3 i)}{(1-3 i)}} \\ &= \sqrt{\frac{6-8 i}{10}}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}-\frac{4}{5} i} \\ & \therefore \quad(x+i y)^2=\frac{3}{5}-\frac{4}{5} i \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x^2-y^2+2 x y i=\frac{3}{5}-\frac{4}{5} i \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x^2-y^2=\frac{3}{5}, 2 x y=\frac{-4}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad\left(x^2+y^2\right)^2=\left(x^2-y^2\right)^2+4 x^2 y^2 \\ &=\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2+\left(\frac{-4}{5}\right)^2=\frac{9}{25}+\frac{16}{25}=1.\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of common roots among the $12^{\text{th }}$ and $30^{\text{th }}$ roots of unity is
questions.solution:
We know that $n^{\text{th }}$ roots of unity $=e^{\frac{i 2 K \pi}{n}}\therefore 12^{\text{th }}$ roots of unity is $e^{i \frac{2 K \pi}{12}}=e^{i \frac{K \pi}{6}}30^{\text{th }}$ roots of unity is $e^{i \frac{2 K \pi}{30}}=e^{i \frac{K \pi}{15}}$
Common values of $\frac{K \pi}{6}$ and $\frac{K \pi}{15}$ are
$0, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{2 \pi}{3}, \pi, \frac{4 \pi}{3}, \frac{5 \pi}{3}\therefore$ Number of common roots $=6$.

questions.q: $x$ and $y$ are two complex numbers such that $|x|=|y|=1$. If $\operatorname{Arg}(x)=2 \alpha, \operatorname{Arg}(y)=3 \beta$ and $\alpha+\beta=\frac{\pi}{36}$, then $x^6 y^4+\frac{1}{x^6 y^4}=$

\end{aligned}$
From (i), take square both sides,
$\begin{aligned}
& \alpha^2+\beta^2+2 \alpha \beta=12 \\
& \alpha^2+\beta^2=12-2 \times 4=12-8=4
\end{aligned}$
Put the values in eq. (iii),
$\begin{aligned}
& \alpha^6+\beta^6=(4)\left[(4)^2-3(4)^2\right] \\
& =4[16-48] \\
& =4 \times(-32)=-128
\end{aligned}$
So, option (d) is correct.

questions.q: If the point& $\left(x, y\right)$ satisfies the equation $\dfrac{x + i\left(x - 2\right)}{3 + i} - i = \dfrac{2y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)}{i - 3}$, then~$x + y =$
questions.solution:
Given,

The point $\left(x, y\right)$ satisfies the equation $\dfrac{x + i\left(x - 2\right)}{3 + i} - i = \dfrac{2y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)}{i - 3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + i\left(x - 2\right)}{\left(3 + i\right)\left(3 - i\right)}\left(3 - i\right) - i = \dfrac{2y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)}{\left(i - 3\right)\left(i + 3\right)}\left(i + 3\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + i\left(x - 2\right)}{10}\left(3 - i\right) - i = \dfrac{2y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)}{- 10}\left(i + 3\right)$

$⇒ \left(x + i\left(x - 2\right)\right)\left(3 - i\right) - 10i = - \left(2y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)\right)\left(i + 3\right)$

$⇒ \left(3x - ix + i\left(x - 2\right)\left(3 - i\right)\right) - 10i = - \left(2iy + 6y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)\left(i + 3\right)\right)$

$⇒ \left(3x - ix + i\left(3x - ix - 6 + 2i\right)\right) - 10i = - \left(2iy + 6y + i\left(i + 3 - 3iy - 9y\right)\right)$

$⇒ \left(3x - ix + 3ix + x - 6i - 2\right) - 10i = - \left(2iy + 6y - 1 + 3i + 3y - 9iy\right)$

$⇒ 4x + 2ix - 13i + 9y - 3 - 7iy = 0$

$⇒ 4x + 9y - 3 + i\left(2x - 13 - 7y\right) = 0$

Now comparing real part and imagenary part we get,

$⇒ 4x + 9y - 3 = 0 . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$ and $⇒ \left(2x - 13 - 7y\right) = 0 . . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now solving equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get, $x = 3 \text{ and } y = - 1$

Then $x + y = 2$

Let

questions.q: $n$ is a positive integer and not a multiple of 3. If $\omega$ is non real cube root of unity, then $\omega^n+\omega^{2 n}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
If $n$ is not a multiple of 3 , then $n=3 K+1 or
n=3 K+2$
where $K \in I$
Case (I) : When, $n=3 K+1, K \in I\begin{aligned}
& \omega^n+\omega^{2 n}=\omega^{3 K+1}+\omega^{2(3 K+1)} \\
& =\omega^{3 k} \cdot \omega+\omega^{6 K} \cdot \omega^2 \\
& \quad\left[\because 1+\omega+\omega^2=0 \text{$ and $} \omega^3=1\right] \\
& =\left(\omega^3\right)^K \cdot \omega+\left(\omega^3\right)^{2 K} \cdot \omega^2 \\
& =\omega+\omega^2=-1
\end{aligned}$
Case (II): When, $n=3 K+2, K \in I\omega^n+\omega^{2 n}=\omega^{3 K+2}+\omega^{2(3 K+2)}\begin{aligned}
& =\omega^{3 K} \cdot \omega^2+\omega^{6 K} \cdot \omega^4 \\
& =\left(\omega^3\right)^K \cdot \omega^2-1\left(\omega^3\right)^{2 K} \cdot \omega \\
& =\omega^2+\omega=-1
\end{aligned}$
In both cases, $\omega^n+\omega^{2 n}=-1, \forall n \notin$ multiple of 3.

questions.q: For $n \in N, {\left(\dfrac{1 + cos\theta + isin\theta}{1 + cos\theta - isin\theta}\right)}^{n} =$
questions.solution:
Given $n \in N, {\left(\dfrac{1 + cos\theta + isin\theta}{1 + cos\theta - isin\theta}\right)}^{n}$

Using $2{cos}^{2}x - 1 = cos2x, 2sinxcosx = sin2x,$ we get

$= {\left(\dfrac{2{cos}^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2} + 2isin\dfrac{\theta}{2}cos\dfrac{\theta}{2}}{2{cos}^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2} - 2isin\dfrac{\theta}{2}cos\dfrac{\theta}{2}}\right)}^{n}$

$= {\left(\dfrac{2cos\dfrac{\theta}{2}\left(cos\dfrac{\theta}{2} + isin\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)}{2cos\dfrac{\theta}{2}\left(cos\dfrac{\theta}{2} - isin\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)}\right)}^{n}$

$= {\left(\dfrac{\left(cos\dfrac{\theta}{2} + isin\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)}{\left(cos\dfrac{\theta}{2} - isin\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)}\right)}^{n}$

Using De-Moivre's theorem i.e. $n \in N, {\left(cosϕ + isinϕ\right)}^{n} = cos\left(nϕ\right) + isin\left(nϕ\right),$ we get

$= \dfrac{\left(cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}{\left(cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) - isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\left(cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}{\left(cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) - isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)} \times \dfrac{\left(cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}{\left(cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}$

$= \dfrac{{\left(cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}^{2}}{\left({cos}^{2}\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) - {i}^{2}{sin}^{2}\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\left({cos}^{2}\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + {i}^{2}{sin}^{2}\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + 2isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}{\left({cos}^{2}\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + {sin}^{2}\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\left({cos}^{2}\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) - {sin}^{2}\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + 2isin\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right)\right)}{\left(1\right)}$

Using ${cos}^{2}x - {sin}^{2}x = cos2x, 2sinxcosx = sin2x,$ we get

$= cos\left(2 \times \dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) + isin\left(2 \times \dfrac{n\theta}{2}\right) = cos\left(n\theta\right) + isin\left(n\theta\right) .$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $a=1+i$ and $z=x+i y$. If the curve $z \bar{z}+a z+\bar{a} \bar{z}-4=0$ is cut by the straight line $(z+\bar{z})-i(z-\bar{z})+2=0$ at two points $A$ and $B$, then the equation of the circle passing through the origin, $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution:
Circle $z \bar{z}+a z+\bar{a} \bar{z}-4=0 \quad\left[\because z \bar{z}=|z|^2\right]\Rightarrow|z|^2+a z+(\overline{a z})-4=0 \quad\left[\because \bar{z}_1 \bar{z}_2=\overline{z_1 z_2}\right]\Rightarrow|z|^2+2 \cdot \operatorname{Re}(a z)-4=0 \quad \ldots(\mathrm{i})[z+\bar{z}=2 \operatorname{Re}(z)]$
Now, given $z=x+i y \Rightarrow|z|^2=x^2+y^2$
and $a=1+i$, then $a z=(1+i)(x+i y)\therefore a z=(x-y)+i(x+y) \Rightarrow \operatorname{Re}(a z)=x-y\therefore$ From Eq. (i), put $\operatorname{Re}(a z)=x-y$
and $\quad|z|^2=x^2+y^2\Rightarrow \quad x^2+y^2+2(x-y)-4=0\Rightarrow S: x^2+y^2+2 x-2 y-4=0 \ldots(\mathrm{ii})$
is a circle and given line
$L: z+\bar{z}-i(z-\bar{z})+2=0\Rightarrow \quad L: 2 \operatorname{Re}(z)-i 2 \operatorname{Im}(z)+2=0\Rightarrow \quad L: 2 x-i(2 y i)+2=0\Rightarrow \quad L: x+y+1=0 \ldots(\mathrm{iii})$
Now, equation of circle passing through point of intersection of circle $S$ and line $L$ is
$S+\lambda L=0\left(x^2+y^2+2 x-2 y-4\right)+\lambda(x+y+1)=0 \ldots(\mathrm{iv})$
Pass through $(0,0)\therefore$ Put in Eq. (iv), we get
$-4+\lambda=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=4$
Now, required circle is
$\Rightarrow \quad x^2+y^2+2 x-2 y-4+4(x+y+1)=0\Rightarrow \quad x^2+y^2+6 x+2 y=0$

questions.solution:
It is given that, if $x^2+x+1=0$, then
$A_r=\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)^3\left(x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}\right)^3\left(x^3+\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^3 \ldots\left(x^r+\frac{1}{x^r}\right)^3$
As, we know that $w$ and $w^2$ are roots of quadratic equation $x^2+x+1=0$, so $w^3=1$ and
$1+w+w^2=0\therefore \quad A_r=\left(w+\frac{1}{w}\right)^3\left(w^2+\frac{1}{w^2}\right)^3\left(w^3+\frac{1}{w^3}\right)^3\ldots\left(w^r+\frac{1}{w^r}\right)^3\therefore \quad A_3=(-1)(-1)(8)=8$
Similarly, $A_6=8^2, A_9=8^3, \ldots$ and so on.
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{A_3}+\frac{1}{A_6}+\frac{1}{A_9}+\frac{1}{A_{12}}+\ldots \infty=\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{8^2}+\frac{1}{8^3}+\frac{1}{8^4}+\ldots \infty=\frac{\frac{1}{8}}{1-\frac{1}{8}}=\frac{1}{7}$

Let $z = x + iy,$ then ${\left(x + iy - 4\right)}^{3} = 8i$

On comparing the real and imaginary parts on both sides of the equation, we get

${\left(x - 4\right)}^{3} - 3\left(x - 4\right){y}^{2} = 0 . . . \left(i\right)$ and

From the equation $\left(i\right),$

${\left(x - 4\right)}^{3} - 3\left(x - 4\right){y}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 4\right)\left[{\left(x - 4\right)}^{2} - 3{y}^{2}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 4\right) = 0$ or ${\left(x - 4\right)}^{2} - 3{y}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ x = 4$ or ${\left(x - 4\right)}^{2} = 3{y}^{2} . . . \left(iii\right)$

On putting, these values in the equation $\left(ii\right),$ we get

$y\left[- {y}^{2} + 3{\left(4 - 4\right)}^{2}\right] = 8$ or $y\left[- {y}^{2} + 3\left(3{y}^{2}\right)\right] = 8$

$⇒ - {y}^{3} = 8$ or $y\left[- {y}^{2} + 9{y}^{2}\right] = 8$

$⇒ y = - 2$ or $8{y}^{3} = 8, ⇒ y = 1 .$

Thus, for $x = 4, y = - 2 .$

Now, for $y = 1,$ from equation $\left(iii\right),$

${\left(x - 4\right)}^{2} = 3$

$⇒ \left(x - 4\right) = \pm \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ x = 4 \pm \sqrt{3} .$

 Hence, the roots of the given equation are $4 - 2i, 4 \pm \sqrt{3} + i .$

And, the given roots are $a - 2i, b + i$ and $c + i .$

On comparing, we get $\sqrt{abc} = \sqrt{4\left(4 + \sqrt{3}\right)\left(4 - \sqrt{3}\right)}$

$⇒ \sqrt{abc} = \sqrt{4\left(16 - 3\right)}$

$⇒ \sqrt{abc} = 2\sqrt{13} .$

questions.solution:
For a complex number $Z=e^{i \theta}$ it is given that
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{3 \cos 3 \theta+2 \cos 2 \theta+5 \cos 5 \theta}{3 \sin 3 \theta+2 \sin 2 \theta+5 \sin 5 \theta}=i \frac{\sum_{r=0}^{10} a_r Z^r}{\sum_{r=0}^{10} b_r Z^r} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\sum_{r=0}^{10} a_r z^r+\sum_{r=0}^{10} b_r z^r}{\sum_{r=0}^{10} a_r z^r-\sum_{r=0}^{10} b_r z^r}=\frac{3 e^{i 3 \theta}+2 e^{i 2 \theta}+5 e^{i 5 \theta}}{3 e^{-i 3 \theta}+2 e^{-i 2 \theta}+5 e^{-i 5 \theta}} \\ & \sum_{r=0}^{10} z^r\left(a_r+b_r\right) \\ & \sum_{r=0}^{10} z^r\left(a_r-b_r\right) \quad=\frac{3 e^{i 3 \theta}+2 e^{i 2 \theta}+5 e^{i 5 \theta}}{3 e^{-i 3 \theta}+2 e^{-i 2 \theta}+5 e^{-i 5 \theta}} \\ & \Rightarrow a_0+b_0=a_1+b_1=a_4+b_4=a_6+b_6 \\ & =a_7+b_7=a_8+b_8 \\ & =a_9+b_9=a_{10}+b_{10}=0 \\ & \text{$ and $} a_2+b_2=2, a_3+b_3=3, a_5+b_5=5\end{aligned}\therefore \quad \frac{\sum_{r=0}^{10}\left(a_r+b_r\right)}{10}=\frac{2+3+5}{10}=1$
