questions.q: If $A + B + C = 4S,$ then $cos ( 2S - A ) + cos ( 2S - B ) - cos ( 2S - C ) - cos2S =$
questions.solution:
Given $A + B + C = 4S .$

Now $cos\left(2S - A\right) + cos\left(2S - B\right) - cos\left(2S - C\right) - cos2S$

$= \left[cos\left(2S - A\right) + cos\left(2S - B\right)\right] - \left[cos\left(2S - C\right) + cos2S\right]$

Using $cos\theta + cosϕ = 2cos\left(\dfrac{\theta + ϕ}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{\theta - ϕ}{2}\right),$

$= 2cos\left(\dfrac{2S - A + 2S - B}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{2S - A - 2S + B}{2}\right) - 2cos\left(\dfrac{2S - C + 2S}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{2S - C - 2S}{2}\right)$

$= 2cos\left(\dfrac{4S - A - B}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right) - 2cos\left(\dfrac{4S - C}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{- C}{2}\right)$

Using the given value and $cos\left(- \theta\right) = cos\theta,$

$= 2cos\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right) - 2cos\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)$

$= 2cos\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\left[cos\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right) - cos\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)\right]$

Using $cos\theta - cosϕ = 2sin\left(\dfrac{\theta + ϕ}{2}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{ϕ - \theta}{2}\right),$

$= 2cos\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\left[2sin\left(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right) + \left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)}{2}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right)}{2}\right)\right]$

$= 2cos\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\left[2sin\left(\dfrac{B - A + A + B}{4}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{A + B - B + A}{4}\right)\right]$

$= 2cos\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\left[2sin\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\right]$

$= 4sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right) .$

questions.q: If $cos\theta = \dfrac{- 3}{5}$ and $\pi < \theta < \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, then $tan\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) =$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{sin\left(x + y\right)}{sin\left(x - y\right)} = \dfrac{a + b}{a - b},$ then $\dfrac{tanx}{tany} =$
questions.solution:
Given, $\dfrac{sin\left(x + y\right)}{sin\left(x - y\right)} = \dfrac{a + b}{a - b}$

$\dfrac{sinx . cosy + cosx . siny}{sinx . cosy - cosx . siny} = \dfrac{a + b}{a - b}$

Use, componendo & dividendo

$\dfrac{sinx . cosy + cosx . siny + sinx . cosy - cosx . siny}{sinx . cosy + cosx . siny - sinx . cosy + cosx . siny} = \dfrac{a + b + a - b}{a + b - a + b}$

$\dfrac{2sinx . cosy}{2cosx . siny} = \dfrac{2a}{2b}$

$\dfrac{\dfrac{sinx}{cosx}}{\dfrac{siny}{cosy}} = \dfrac{a}{b}$

$\dfrac{tanx}{tany} = \dfrac{a}{b}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x \ne - y$ and $sinx + siny = 3\left(cosy - cosx\right),$ then $tan\left(x - y\right) =$
questions.solution:
Given, $sinx + siny = 3\left(cosy - cosx\right)$

$2sin\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) . cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) = 3 \times 2sin\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) . sin\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)$

$cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) = 3 \times sin\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)$

$tan\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Now, $tan\left(x - y\right) = \dfrac{2tan\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)}{1 - {\left[tan\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)\right]}^{2}}$

$tan\left(x - y\right) = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{1}{3}}{1 - {\left[\dfrac{1}{3}\right]}^{2}}$

$tan\left(x - y\right) = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{1}{3}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{9}}$

$tan\left(x - y\right) = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{1}{3}}{\dfrac{8}{9}}$

$tan\left(x - y\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $90 ° < A < 180 °$ and $sinA = \dfrac{4}{5},$ then $tan\dfrac{A}{2} =$
questions.solution:
Given,& $90 ° < A < 180 °$

$sinA = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$sinA = \dfrac{2tan\dfrac{A}{2}}{1 + {tan}^{2}\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$\dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{2tan\dfrac{A}{2}}{1 + {tan}^{2}\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$4{tan}^{2}\dfrac{A}{2} - 10tan\dfrac{A}{2} + 4 = 0$

$2{tan}^{2}\dfrac{A}{2} - 5tan\dfrac{A}{2} + 2 = 0$

$2{tan}^{2}\dfrac{A}{2} - 4tan\dfrac{A}{2} - tan\dfrac{A}{2} + 2 = 0$

$2tan\dfrac{A}{2}\left(tan\dfrac{A}{2} - 2\right) - 1\left(tan\dfrac{A}{2} - 2\right) = 0$

$\left(tan\dfrac{A}{2} - 2\right)\left(2tan\dfrac{A}{2} - 1\right) = 0$

$tan\dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$~is& not possible in the given interval

Hence,& $tan\dfrac{A}{2} = 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{n}\left[sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} + sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left(3 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) + sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left(3 + \dfrac{2}{n}\right) +... + sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right] =$
questions.solution:
The given limit is

$l = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{n}\left[sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} + sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left(3 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) + sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left(3 + \dfrac{2}{n}\right) + . . . + sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]$

$⇒ l = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{n}\left[sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} + sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{12n}\right) + sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{2}{12n}\right) + . . . + sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \left(n\right)\dfrac{\pi}{12n}\right)\right]$

We know that

$sin\alpha + sin\left(\alpha + \beta\right) + sin\left(\alpha + 2\beta\right) + . . . + sin\left(\alpha + \left(N - 1\right)\beta\right) = \dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{N\beta}{2}\right)sin\left(\alpha + \dfrac{\left(N - 1\right)\beta}{2}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{\beta}{2}\right)} .$

Here, $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{4}, \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{12n}, N = n + 1 .$

$⇒ l = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{n}\left[\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)\pi}{24n}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + n \times \dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)}\right]$

$⇒ l = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{n}\left[\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24} + \dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)\left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)}\right)}\right]$

$⇒ l = \lim_{n \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{24sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24} + \dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{24}\right)}{\left(\pi\right)\left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24n}\right)}\right)}\right]$

Using $\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{sinx}{x}\right) = 1$ and $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{n}\right) = 0,$

$⇒ l = \left[\dfrac{24sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{24}\right)}{\pi}\right]$

Using $2sinAsinB = cos\left(A - B\right)cos\left(A + B\right),$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{12}{\pi}\left[cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{24} - \dfrac{\pi}{24}\right) - cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{24} + \dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)\right]$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{12}{\pi}\left[cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right]$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{12}{\pi}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{12}{\pi}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{2} - 1}{2}\right] = \dfrac{6\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)}{\pi} .$

questions.q: Let $ACB$ be a triangle with right-angle at $C.$ Let $AB = 29$ units, $BC = 21$ units and $ABC = \theta.$ Then $\cos^{2}\theta - \sin^{2}\theta =$
questions.solution:

questions.solution:
Given that

$A + B + C = 270 °$

$⇒ cos2A + cos2B + cos2C + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= cos2A + \left[2cos\left(\dfrac{2B + 2C}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{2B - 2C}{2}\right)\right] + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= cos2A + 2cos ( B + C ) cos ( B - C ) + 4sinAsinBsinc$

$= cos2A + 2cos ( 270 ° - A ) cos ( B - C ) + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= cos2A - 2sinAcos ( B - C ) + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= 1 - 2\sin^{2}A - 2sin\left(270 ° - \left(B + C\right)\right)cos\left(B - C\right) + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= 1 - 2\sin^{2}A - 2sinAcos ( B - C ) + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= 1 - 2sinA\left(sinA + cos\left(B - C\right)\right) + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= 1 - 2sinA\left(- cos ( B + C ) + cos ( B - C )\right) + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= 1 - 2sinA\left(2sin\left(\dfrac{B + C + B - C}{2}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{( B + C ) - ( B - C )}{2}\right)\right) + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= 1 - 2sinA ( 2sinBsinC ) + 4sinAsinBsinC$

$= 1$

And

Consider,

$⇒ A\left(1\right)A\left(6\right) + A\left(2\right)A\left(3\right) = \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{6}\alpha + {cos}^{6}\alpha\right) + \left({sin}^{2}\alpha + {cos}^{2}\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{3}\alpha + {cos}^{3}\alpha\right)$

$= \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{4}\alpha\left(1 - {cos}^{2}\alpha\right) + {cos}^{4}\alpha\left(1 - {sin}^{2}\alpha\right)\right) + \left({sin}^{3}\alpha + {cos}^{3}\alpha\right)$

$= \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{4}\alpha - {sin}^{4}\alpha{cos}^{2}\alpha + {cos}^{4}\alpha - {cos}^{4}\alpha{sin}^{2}\alpha\right) + \left({sin}^{3}\alpha + {cos}^{3}\alpha\right)$

$= \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{4}\alpha + {cos}^{4}\alpha\right) - \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right){sin}^{4}\alpha{cos}^{2}\alpha - \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right){cos}^{4}\alpha{sin}^{2}\alpha + \left({sin}^{3}\alpha + {cos}^{3}\alpha\right)$

$= \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{4}\alpha + {cos}^{4}\alpha\right) - \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right){sin}^{2}\alpha{cos}^{2}\alpha\left({sin}^{2}\alpha + {cos}^{2}\alpha\right) + \left({sin}^{3}\alpha + {cos}^{3}\alpha\right)$

$= \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{4}\alpha + {cos}^{4}\alpha\right) - \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{2}\alpha\right)\left({cos}^{2}\alpha\right) + \left({sin}^{3}\alpha + {cos}^{3}\alpha\right)$

$= \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{4}\alpha + {cos}^{4}\alpha\right) + {sin}^{3}\alpha\left(1 - {cos}^{2}\alpha\right) + {cos}^{3}\alpha\left(1 - {sin}^{2}\alpha\right)$

$= \left(sin\alpha + cos\alpha\right)\left({sin}^{4}\alpha + {cos}^{4}\alpha\right) + \left({sin}^{5}\alpha + {cos}^{5}\alpha\right)$

$= A\left(1\right)A\left(4\right) + A\left(2\right)A\left(5\right)$

$∴ A\left(1\right)A\left(4\right) + A\left(2\right)A\left(5\right) = A\left(1\right)A\left(6\right) + A\left(2\right)A\left(3\right)$

$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Given, } \quad \sin \theta+\cos \theta=p \\ & \text{$ and $} \quad \sin ^3 \theta+\cos ^3 \theta=q \\ & \Rightarrow \quad(\sin \theta+\cos \theta) \\ & \quad\left(\sin ^2 \theta-\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\right)=q\end{aligned}$
\Rightarrow \quad p(1-\sin $\theta \cdot \cos \theta)=$ q [From Eq. (i) and $\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta=1$ ] $\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow& 1-\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta=\frac{q}{p}\\
\Rightarrow \quad & \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta=1-\frac{q}{p}
\end{aligned}$ On squaring both sides of Eq. (i), we get $\begin{aligned}& \sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta+2 \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta= p^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1+2\left(1-\frac{q}{p}\right)= p^2 \quad \text{ [from Eq. (iii)] }\\
& \Rightarrow \quad p+2(p-q)=p³ \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3 p-2 q=p³ \\
& \Rightarrow \quad p³-3 p=-2 q \\
& \Rightarrow \quad p\left( p^2-3\right)=-2 q \\
&
\end{aligned}
$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ LHS }=\tan x+\tan \left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+\tan \left(x+\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right) \\ & =\tan x+\frac{\tan x+\sqrt{3}}{1-\sqrt{3} \tan x}+\frac{\tan x-\sqrt{3}}{1+\sqrt{3} \tan x} \\ & =\tan x+\frac{\left[\begin{array}{c}(\tan x+\sqrt{3})(1+\sqrt{3} \tan x) \\ +(\tan x-\sqrt{3})(1-\sqrt{3} \tan x)\end{array}\right]}{1-3 \tan ^2 x} \\ & =\frac{\left[\begin{array}{c}\tan x\left(1-3 \tan ^2 x\right)+\tan x+\sqrt{3} \\ +\sqrt{3} \tan ^2 x+3 \tan x+\tan x-\sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} \tan ^2 x+3 \tan x\end{array}\right]}{1-3 \tan ^2 x} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\tan x\left(1-3 \tan ^2 x\right)+8 \tan x}{1-3 \tan ^2 x}=3 \quad \text{ (given) } \\ & \Rightarrow \tan x\left(1-3 \tan ^2 x\right)+8 \tan x \\ & =3\left(1-3 \tan ^2 x\right) \\ & \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \tan x\left(9-3 \tan ^2 x\right)=3\left(1-3 \tan ^2 x\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \tan x\left(3-\tan ^2 x\right)=1-3 \tan ^2 x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{3 \tan x-\tan ^3 x}{1-3 \tan ^2 x}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \tan 3 x=1\end{aligned}$

Now, $|(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \vec{c} \|(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}) \vec{b}-(\vec{c} \vec{b}) \vec{a}|=0$ And, $|(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c}|=|\vec{a} \| \vec{b}||\vec{c}|\begin{aligned} & \quad[\because \vec{a} \perp \vec{b} \Rightarrow|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|] \\ & \therefore|(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c}|+|(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \vec{c}|=|\vec{a}||\vec{b} \| \vec{c}|\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
$\because|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|^2=|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2+2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\begin{aligned} & \therefore 37=9+16+2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} \\ & \Rightarrow 12=2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=6 \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \cos \theta=6 \\ & \Rightarrow 3 \cdot 4 \cos \theta=6 \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=60^{{}^{\circ}} \\ & \therefore|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2=|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2-2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} \\ & \Rightarrow k^2=9+16-12=13 \end{aligned}$
Now, $\frac{4}{13}(k \sin \theta)^2=\frac{4}{13} \cdot k^2 \sin ^2 \theta$=$\frac{4}{13}\cdot 13 \sin ^2 60^{{}^{\circ}}=4 $\cdot $\frac{3}{4}=3 .$

questions.q: The volume of the tetrahedron with $\hat{i}-\lambda \hat{j}+\hat{k}, \lambda \hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\lambda \hat{k}$ as coterminous edges is 2. If $\lambda$ is an integer, then $|\lambda \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \lambda \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}|=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{6}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & -\lambda & 1 \\ \lambda & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & \lambda\end{array}\right|=2 \\ & \Rightarrow\left|(-\lambda+1)+\lambda\left(\lambda^2+1\right)+1(\lambda+1)\right|=12 \\ & \Rightarrow 2+\lambda\left(\lambda^2+1\right)=12 \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda\left(\lambda^2+1\right)=10=2 \times 5 \\ & \therefore \quad \lambda=2. \\ & \therefore|\lambda \hat{i}-3 \lambda \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}|=|2 \hat{i}-6 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}| \\ & =\sqrt{2^2+(-6)^2+3^2}=\sqrt{49}=7.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\overrightarrow{O A}=\hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+\hat{k}, \overrightarrow{O B}=\hat{i}+3 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{O C}=4 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+5 \hat{k}$ be the position vectors of three points $A, B$ and $C$. Let $P$ be the point which divides $A B$ in the ratio $2: 1$. If $1, m, n$ are the direction cosines of the vector $\overrightarrow{P C}$, then $1+3 m+2 n=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \vec{r}=\frac{2(\overrightarrow{O B})+1(\overrightarrow{O A})}{2+1}=\frac{2 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}-4 \hat{k}+\hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+\hat{k}}{3} \\ & =\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k} \\ & \overrightarrow{P C}=\overrightarrow{O C}-\vec{r}=(4 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+5 \hat{k})-(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}) \\ & =3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k} \\ & \therefore \quad \text{ D.C.$ of $} \overrightarrow{P C}: \\ & \left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{3^2+2^2+6^2}}, \frac{2}{\sqrt{3^2+2^2+6^2}}, \frac{6}{\sqrt{3^2+2^2+6^2}}\right) \\ & \equiv\left(\frac{3}{7}, \frac{2}{7}, \frac{6}{7}\right) \equiv(l, m, n) \\ & \therefore \quad l+3 m+2 n=\frac{3}{7}+\frac{6}{7}+\frac{12}{7}=3 .\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\bar{a}=\lambda \bar{i}+3 \bar{j}+4 \bar{k}, \bar{b}=3 \bar{i}-\bar{j}+\lambda \bar{k}$ and $\bar{c}=\lambda \bar{i}+\bar{j}-3 \bar{k}$ be three vectors for some integer $\lambda$. If the volume of the parallelepiped with $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ as coterminus edges is 61 cubic units, then the number of possible values of $\lambda$ is
questions.solution:
Volume of parallelopiped $=\left[$\begin{array}{lll}$\vec{a}$ & $\vec{b}$ & $\vec{c}$\end{array}$\right]\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow & \left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\lambda & 3 & 4 \\
3 & -1 & \lambda \\
\lambda & 1 & -3
\end{array}\right|=61 \\
\Rightarrow & \lambda(3-\lambda)-3\left(-9-\lambda^2\right)+4(3+\lambda)=61 \\
\Rightarrow & 3 \lambda-\lambda^2+27+3 \lambda^2+12+4 \lambda=61 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 \lambda^2+7 \lambda-22=0 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 \lambda^2+11 \lambda-4 \lambda-22=0 \\
\Rightarrow & (2 \lambda+11)(\lambda-2)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \lambda=\frac{-11}{2}, \lambda=2
\end{aligned}\because \lambda$ is integer, $\therefore \lambda=2$.
Number of possible value is one.

If the area of $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$ is $5 \sqrt{6}$ sq. units, then the sum of the absolute values of $a, b, c$ is
questions.solution: $a \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+c \hat{k}=d \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}+3 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-2 \hat{k}\begin{aligned} & a \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+c \hat{k}=(d+3) \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \\ & \therefore \quad a=d+3 \Rightarrow d=a-3 \\ & \quad b=4 \\ & \quad c=2\end{aligned}$ Area of $\begin{aligned} \Delta & =\frac{1}{2}|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{lll}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ a & b & c \\ d & 3 & 4\end{array}\right|=5 \sqrt{6} .\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow|(4 b-3 c) \hat{i}+(c d-4 a) \hat{j}+(3 a-b d) \hat{k}|=10 \sqrt{6} \\ & \Rightarrow|10 \hat{i}+(2 d-4 a) \hat{j}+(3 a-4 d) \hat{k}|=10 \sqrt{6} \\ & \Rightarrow|10 \hat{i}+(-2 a-6) \hat{j}+(12-a) \hat{k}|=10 \sqrt{6} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 10^2+(-2 a-6)^2+(12-a)^2=600 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 4 a^2+36+24 a+144+a^2-24 a=500 \\ & \Rightarrow 5 a^2=320 \Rightarrow a^2=64 \\ & \therefore|a|=8 \\ & \therefore|a|+|b|+|c|=8+4+2=14 .\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
$\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are non collinear vectors and $(\vec{c} \cdot \vec{c}) \vec{a}=\vec{c}$.
If $(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}) \vec{b}-(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) \vec{c}+(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) \vec{b}=(4-2 \beta-\sin \alpha) \vec{b}+\left(\beta^2-1\right) \vec{c}$ then $\sin (\alpha+\beta)=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \text{c}=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{c} \cdot \vec{c}=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2 \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \vec{c} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{c}|^2(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}})=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=|\mathrm{c}|^2 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}=1(i) \\ \\ & \because(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}-(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=(4-2 \beta-\sin \alpha) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+\left(\beta^2-1\right) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \\ \\ & (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) \vec{b}-(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) \vec{c}=(4-2 \beta-\sin \alpha) \vec{b}+\left(\beta^2-1\right) \vec{c} \\ \\ & \therefore \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=4-2 \beta-\sin \alpha (ii)\\ \\ & \&-\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=\beta^2-1 \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=1-\beta^2 (iii) \\ \end{aligned}$
From (i), (ii) & (iii):
$\begin{aligned} \\ & 1-\beta^2+1=4-2 \beta-\sin \alpha \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \beta^2-2 \beta+2-\sin \alpha=0 \\ \end{aligned}$
Let $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow \sin \alpha=1$
$\Rightarrow \beta^2-2 \beta+1=0 \Rightarrow(\beta-1)^2=0 \Rightarrow \beta=1$
Now, $\sin (\alpha+\beta)=\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+1\right)=\cos 1$

questions.q: $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are three-unit vectors such that $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|=1$ and $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$. If $\vec{c}$ makes angles $\alpha, \beta$ with $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ respectively, then $\cos \alpha+\cos \beta=$
questions.solution:
$|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|=1\begin{aligned}
& \vec{a} \perp \vec{b} \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=0 \\
& |\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}|=1 \\
& \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=|\vec{c}||\vec{a}| \cos \alpha \\
& \therefore \quad \cos \alpha=\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \vec{c} \cdot \vec{b}=|\vec{c}||\vec{b}| \cos \beta \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \cos \beta=c \cdot b \Rightarrow|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|^2=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}) \cdot(\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c})=1 \\
& \Rightarrow|\vec{a}|^2+\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+|\vec{b}|^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3+2 \cos \alpha+2 \cos \beta=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2(\cos \alpha+\cos \beta)=-2 \\
& \Rightarrow \cos \alpha+\cos \beta=-1 \end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\cos \theta=\frac{(4 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+2 \hat{k}) \cdot(\hat{i}+3 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k})}{\sqrt{21} \times \sqrt{14}}=\frac{-3}{7 \sqrt{6}}\sin \theta=\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{-3}{7 \sqrt{6}}\right)^2}=\sqrt{1-\frac{9}{49 \times 6}}=\frac{\sqrt{285}}{7 \sqrt{6}}\begin{aligned} & \cos \theta < 0 \Rightarrow \theta \in\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right) \Rightarrow \sin \theta>0 \\ & \sin 2 \theta=2 \cos \theta \cdot \sin \theta \\ & =2 \times\left(\frac{-3}{7 \sqrt{6}}\right) \times \frac{\sqrt{285}}{7 \sqrt{6}}=\frac{-\sqrt{285}}{49}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $|\vec{a}|=1,|\vec{b}|=2,|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}|^2=20$ then $(\vec{a}, \vec{b})=$
questions.solution: $|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}|^2=20\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad(\vec{a}-\vec{b}) \cdot(\vec{a}-\vec{b})+(\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}) \cdot(\vec{a}+2 \vec{b})=20 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad|\vec{a}|^2-2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+|\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{a}|^2+4 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+4|\vec{b}|^2=20 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2|\vec{a}|^2+5|\vec{b}|^2+2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=20 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2(1)^2+5(2)^2+2(1)(2) \cos \theta=20 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 22+4 \cos \theta=20 \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{-1}{2} \\ & \therefore \quad \theta=\frac{2 \pi}{3}.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\mathrm{ABC}$ be a triangle and $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ be the position vectors of $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ respectively, Let $\mathrm{D}$ divide $\mathrm{BC}$ in the ratio $3: 1$ internally and $\mathrm{E}$ divide $\mathrm{AD}$ in the ratio $4: 1$ internally. Let $\mathrm{BE}$ meet $\mathrm{AC}$ in $\mathrm{F}$. If $\mathrm{E}$ divides $\mathrm{BF}$ in the ratio $3: 2$ internally then the position vector of $\mathrm{F}$ is
questions.solution:
Here we are given that $\overline{\mathrm{OA}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}, \overline{\mathrm{OB}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}, \overline{\mathrm{OC}}=\overline{\mathrm{c}}$
Now P.V of D i.e $\overline{\mathrm{OD}}=\frac{1 \times \overline{\mathrm{OB}}+3 \times \overline{\mathrm{OC}}}{1+3}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \overline{\mathrm{OD}}=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}}{4} \\ \\ & \overline{\mathrm{OE}}=\frac{4 \overline{\mathrm{OD}}+\overline{\mathrm{OA}}}{4+1}=\frac{\frac{4(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}})}{4}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}}{5} \Rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{OE}}=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}}{5} \\ \end{aligned}$
Now, $\overline{\mathrm{OE}}=\frac{2 \overline{\mathrm{OB}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{OF}}}{2+3}$
$\Rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{OF}}=\frac{5 \overline{\mathrm{OE}}-2 \overline{\mathrm{OB}}}{3}$
$\Rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{OF}}=\frac{\frac{5(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}}{5}-\overline{2 \mathrm{ b}}}{3}$
$\Rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{OF}}=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}}{3}$
\Rightarrow P.V.$ of F is\frac{\vec{a}-\vec{b}+3 \vec{c}}{3}$

questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are real numbers such that $\left(\frac{7}{3}+\beta\right) \bar{i}-\bar{j}+(\alpha+\gamma) \bar{k}=\frac{5}{3}(\alpha \bar{i}+\bar{j}-\bar{k})+\beta(2 \bar{j}+\bar{k})+(\bar{i}+\gamma \bar{j}+3 \bar{k}), \text{ then } 5 \alpha-9 \beta+13 \gamma=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \therefore\left(\frac{7}{3}+\beta\right) \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+(\alpha+\gamma) \hat{\mathrm{k}}=\frac{5}{3}(\alpha \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\ \\ & +\mathrm{B}(2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})+(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{y} \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{7}{3}+\beta\right) \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+(\alpha+\gamma) \hat{\mathrm{k}}=\left(\frac{5}{3} \alpha+1\right) \hat{\mathrm{i}} \\ \\ & +\left(\frac{5}{3}+2 \beta+\gamma\right) \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\left(\frac{-5}{3}+\beta+3\right) \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ \end{aligned}$
comparing both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \frac{7}{3}+\beta=\frac{5}{3} \alpha+1 \Rightarrow 5 \alpha-3 \beta=4 \\ \\ & -1=\frac{5}{3}+2 \beta+\gamma \Rightarrow 2 \beta+\gamma=\frac{-8}{3} \\ \\ & \alpha+\gamma=\frac{-5}{3}+\beta+3 \Rightarrow \alpha-\beta+\gamma=\frac{4}{3} \\ \end{aligned}$
solving equations (i), (ii), and (iii), we get
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \alpha=0, \beta=\frac{-4}{3}, \gamma=0 \\ \\ & \therefore 5 \alpha-9 \beta+13 \gamma=12 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $a, b, c$ be three vectors such that $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=5$ and $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}|^2+|\vec{b}+\vec{c}-\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{c}+\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2=50$ then $\vec{a} \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=$

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}=\vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}=\vec{c} \cdot \vec{c}=5\therefore|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}|=\sqrt{5}$
also $|\vec{x}|^2=\vec{x} \cdot \vec{x}\begin{aligned} & |\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}|^2=(\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}) \cdot(\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}) \\ & =\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}+\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{b} \\ & \quad-\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}-\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}-\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{c}\end{aligned}=15+2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-2 \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}-2 \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}$ ...(i)
$\begin{aligned} & |\vec{b}+\vec{c}-\vec{a}|^2=(\vec{b}+\vec{c}-\vec{a}) \cdot(\vec{b}+\vec{c}-\vec{a}) \\ & \quad \vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}-\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{c} \\ & \quad-\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}-\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}\end{aligned}=15-2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+2 \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}-2 \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}$ ...(ii)
$|\vec{c}+\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2=(\vec{c}+\vec{a}-\vec{b}) \cdot(\vec{c}+\vec{a}-\vec{b})=15-2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-2 \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+2 \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}$ ...(iii)
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ (i) }+ \text{ (ii) }+ \text{ (iii) } \\ & |\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}|^2+|\vec{b}+\vec{c}-\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{c}+\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2 \\ & =45-2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})=50 \\ & \therefore \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=\frac{-5}{2}\end{aligned}$

Given $\vec{a}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}, \vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$
Then, $\vec{x}=\left(\frac{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|^2}\right) \cdot \vec{b}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \vec{x}=\left(\frac{(2 \hat{i}+\hat{y}-\hat{k}) \cdot(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k})}{\left(\sqrt{\left((1)^2+(-1)^2+(3)^2\right)}\right)^2}\right) \cdot(\vec{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \\ \\ & \vec{x}=\left(\frac{2-1+3}{(1+1+9)}\right)(\vec{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \\ \\ & \vec{x}=\frac{-2}{11}(\vec{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \\ \\ & \vec{y}=\left(\frac{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}}{|\vec{a}|^2}\right) \cdot \vec{a} \cdot \\ \\ & \vec{y}=\left(\frac{(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}) \cdot(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k})}{\left((2)^2+(1)^2+(-1)^2\right)}\right) \cdot(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}) \\ \\ & \vec{y}=\left(\frac{2-1-3}{4+1+1}\right) \cdot(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}) \\ \\ & \vec{y}=\frac{-2}{6}(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})=\frac{-1}{3}(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}) . \\ \end{aligned}$
Angle between $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}$ is $\cos \theta=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}}{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}| \cdot|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|}$.
$\cos \theta=\frac{(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \cdot(\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}})}{\sqrt{6} \sqrt{11}}=\frac{2-1-3}{\sqrt{66}}=\frac{-2}{\sqrt{66}}$
Take square both sides
$\cos ^2 \theta=\frac{4}{66}$
Now, $\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{y}^2=\frac{4}{11}(1+1+9)+\frac{1}{9}(4+1+1)$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & x^2+y^2=\frac{34 \times 2}{33 \times 2}=\frac{68}{66} \\ \\ & x^2+y^2=17 \times \frac{4}{66}=17 \cos ^2 \theta \quad\{\text{$ from $(i) }\} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Let $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ be three unit vectors satisfying $|\bar{a}-\bar{b}|^2+|\bar{a}-\bar{c}|^2=10$. Then
Statement (I) : $|\bar{a}+2 \bar{b}|^2+|2 \bar{a}+\bar{c}|^2=2$.
Statement (II) : $|2 \bar{a}+3 \bar{b}|^2+|3 \bar{a}+2 \bar{c}|^2=10$.
Which of the above statements is (are) true?
options: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
Statement II is true but Statement I is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.solution: Given vector experssion is $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2=10 \begin{aligned} \\ & |\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|^2-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=10 \\ \\ & -2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}})+4=10 \\ \\ & -2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}})=6 \\ \end{aligned}$From statement (I): $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|^2+|^{2} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2=2$Take L.H.S,$\begin{aligned} \\ & \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2+4|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|^2+4 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+4|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2+4 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 1+4+4 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}})+4+1 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 4 \times(-3)+8+2\{\text{$ from $(i) }\} \Rightarrow-12+10=-2 \\ \end{aligned}$So, statement I is false.Now, take statement (II): $|2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|^2+|^{3} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2$ Take L.H.S.$\begin{aligned} \\ & |2 \vec{a}+3 \vec{b}|^2+|^{3} \vec{a}+2 \vec{c}|^2 \\ \\ & =4|\vec{a}|^2+9|\vec{b}|^2+\left.|12 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+9| \vec{a}\right|^2+4|\vec{c}|^2+12 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} \\ \\ & =4.1+9.1+12 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+9.1+4.1+12 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} \\ \\ & =12 \vec{a}(\vec{b}+\vec{c})+26=12 \times-2+26=2 \\ \end{aligned}$So statement II is also false.Therefore, option (d) is correct.

questions.q: If $A\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right), B\left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right), C  \left(-4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$ and $D  \left(- \overset{^}{i} -2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$ are four points in space such that $\overset{→}{AB} = x\overset{→}{AC} + y\overset{→}{AD}$ for some real numbers $x \ne 0, y \ne 0$ then $17\left(\lambda +9\right) =$
questions.solution:
Given,

$A\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right), B\left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right), C\left(- 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$ and $D\left(- \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$ are four points in space such that $\overset{\to}{AB} = x\overset{\to}{AC} + y\overset{\to}{AD}$

So, $\overset{\to}{AB} = x\overset{\to}{AC} + y\overset{\to}{AD}$

$⇒ \left(\lambda - 2\right)\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k} = x\left(- 6\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) + y\left(- 3\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Now on comparing coefficient $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k}$ we get,

$⇒ \left(\lambda - 2\right) = - 6x - 3y . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ 4 = 2x - 3y . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ 5 = 3x + 4y . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

Now solving $\left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$ we get,

$x = \dfrac{31}{17} \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 2}{17}$

Now putting the value of $x \text{ and } y$ in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\left(\lambda - 2\right) = - 6 \times \dfrac{31}{17} - 3 \times \dfrac{\left(- 2\right)}{17}$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{- 146}{17}$

Then $17\left(\lambda + 9\right) = 17\left(\dfrac{- 146}{17} + 9\right) = 7$

questions.q: In a triangle $ABC, D$ and $E$ divide the sides $BC$ and $CA$ in the ratio $2: 1$ respectively. If $P$ is the point of intersection of $AD$ and $BE$ then the ratio in which $P$ divides $AD$ is
questions.solution:
We have,

Let $AD$ and $BE$ intersect at $P$.
Let $A, B, C, D, E, P$ have position vectors $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}, \overset{→}{c}, \overset{→}{d}, \overset{→}{e}, \overset{→}{p}$ respectively.

$D$ and $E$ divide segments $BC$ and $CA$ internally in the ratio $2: 1$.

By the section formula for internal division,
$\overset{→}{d} = \dfrac{2 \times \overset{→}{c} + 1 \times \overset{→}{b}}{2 + 1}$

$⇒ 3\overset{→}{d} = 2\overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{b}... \left(1\right)$

And,

$\overset{→}{e} = \dfrac{2\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{c}}{2 + 1}$

$⇒ 3\overset{→}{e} = 2\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{c}.... \left(2\right)$

From $\left(1\right)$,

$3\overset{→}{d} - \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{→}{c}..... \left(3\right)$

From $\left(2\right)$,

$3\overset{→}{e} - 2\overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{c}$

$⇒ 2\overset{→}{c} = 6\overset{→}{e} - 4\overset{→}{a}.... \left(4\right)$

Equating both values of $2\overset{→}{c}$, we get

$6\overset{→}{e} - 4\overset{→}{a} = 3\overset{→}{d} - \overset{→}{b}$

$⇒ 6\overset{→}{e} + \overset{→}{b} = 4\overset{→}{a} + 3\overset{→}{d}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4\overset{→}{a} + 3\overset{→}{d}}{4 + 3} = \dfrac{6\overset{→}{e} + \overset{→}{b}}{6 + 1}$

LHS is the position vector of the point which divides segment $AD$ internally in the ratio $3: 4$

RHS is the position vector of the point which divides segment $BE$ internally in the ratio $6: 1$.

But $P$ is the point of intersection of $AD$ and $BE$.

$∴ P$ divides $AD$ internally in the ratio $3: 4$.

questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{b}$ are two vectors such that $\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + p\overset{^}{k}, \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = 7$

Now given $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 4$

So, applying the formula we get,

$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 4 ⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|cos\theta = 4$

$⇒ \sqrt{8 + p^{2}} \times 7cos\theta = 4$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{4}{7\sqrt{8 + p^{2}}}$

$⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{\left(7\sqrt{8 + p^{2}}\right)2 - {4}^{2}}{7\sqrt{8 + p^{2}}} = \dfrac{49p^{2} + 376}{7\sqrt{8 + p^{2}}}$

Now also given~$\left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| = 5\sqrt{17}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|sin\theta = 5\sqrt{17}$

$⇒ \sqrt{8 + p^{2}} \times 7 \times \dfrac{49p^{2} + 376}{7\sqrt{8 + p^{2}}} = 5\sqrt{17}$

$⇒ \sqrt{49p^{2} + 376} = 5\sqrt{17}$

$⇒ 49p^{2} + 376 = 25 \times 17$

$⇒ 49p^{2} = 49$

$⇒ p = \pm 1$

For non-collinear vectors $\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c},|\mathbf{c}| \neq 0$, it is given that, $(\mathbf{c} \cdot \mathbf{c}) \mathbf{a}=\mathbf{c} \Rightarrow \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}=1\ldots(\mathrm{i})$

We are given that& $A\left(\overset{→}{a}\right), B \left(\overset{→}{b}\right),C \left(\overset{→}{c}\right)$& $D\left(\overset{→}{d}\right) are four concyclic points such that

$ x\overset{→}{a} + y\overset{→}{b} + z\overset{→}{c} + t\overset{→}{d} = \overset{→}{0} . . . $\left(\text{i}\right)$

Now, we know that angle subtended by chord on same side of circle are equal therefore

$∠ A = ∠ C ∠ B = ∠ D ∠ P = ∠ P$

Hence, by $AAA$

$△ APD ∆ CPB$

So,

\dfrac{AP}{CP} = \dfrac{PD}{PB}$

$⇒ \dfrac{r - \overset{→}{a}}{r - \overset{→}{c}} = \dfrac{r - \overset{→}{d}}{r - \overset{→}{b}} . . . \left(\text{iii}\right)$

Now, equation of line $AB$

$\overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{a} + ${k}_{1} $\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right)$⇒ \overset{→}{r} - \overset{→}{a} = {k}_{1} $\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) . . . \left(\text{iv}\right)$

$\overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{b} + ${k}_{2} $\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right)$⇒ \overset{→}{r} - \overset{→}{b} = {k}_{2} $\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) . . . \left(\text{v}\right)$

Now, equation of line $CD$

$\overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{c} + {k}_{3}\left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{d}\right)⇒ \overset{→}{r} - \overset{→}{c} = {k}_{3} \left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{d}\right) . . . \left(\text{vi}\right)

$\overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{d} + ${k}_{4} \left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{d}\right)⇒ \overset{→}{r} - \overset{→}{d} = {k}_{4} \left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{d}\right) . . . \left(\text{vii}\right)

Putting these values in \left(\text{iii}\right),$ we get

${k}_{1}{k}_{2}\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right)2 = {k}_{3}{k}_{4} \left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{d}\right)2 . . . \left(\text{viii}\right)$

$ x = {k}_{2}, y = 1 - {k}_{2}, z = - {k}_{4}, t = - 1 + {k}_{4} . . . . \left($ B\right)$

Combining \left(A\right) & \left($ B\right)$, we get

${k}_{1} = y, {k}_{2} = x, {k}_{3} = t, {k}_{4} = - z$

$- $xy\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right)2 = - $zt $\left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{d}\right)2$

If $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are two vectors such that $\mathbf{p}=\mathbf{a}-2 \mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{q}=2 \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$, then the angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is
questions.solution:
$\because \mathbf{p}=\mathbf{a}-2 \mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{q}=2 \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$
So,
$\begin{aligned} 5 \mathbf{a} & =\mathbf{p}+2 \mathbf{q}=(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}})+2(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ & =5 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \mathbf{a}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\frac{\hat{\mathbf{k}}}{5}$
Similarly, $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{q}-2 \mathbf{a}=(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}})-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\frac{2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}}{5}=-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\frac{3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}}{5}$
So, angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is
$\begin{aligned} & \theta=\cos ^{-1}\left|\frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{a}| \mid \mathbf{b} \|}\right|=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{\frac{3}{25}}{\frac{\sqrt{26}}{5} \times \frac{\sqrt{34}}{5}}\right) \\ & =\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{2 \sqrt{13 \times 17}}\right)=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{2 \sqrt{221}}\right)\end{aligned}$
Hence, option (a) is correct.

So,
$\mathbf{P Q}=\mathbf{O Q}-\mathbf{O P}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\quad \mathbf{R S}=\mathbf{O S}-\mathbf{O R}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
As $\frac{a_1}{a_2}=\frac{b_1}{b_2}=\frac{c_1}{c_2}\therefore$ Angle between $\mathbf{P Q}$ and $\mathbf{R S}$ is 0 . Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.q: If $\mathbf{a}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}, \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=1$ and $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}=\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}$, then $\mathbf{b}=$
questions.solution:
Let vector $\mathbf{b}=b_1 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+b_2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+b_3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$, then
$\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=b_1+b_2+b_3=1$ (given )
and $\begin{aligned} \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}=\left(b_3-b_2\right) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\left(b_1-b_3\right) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+ & \left(b_2-b_1\right) \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ & =\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}} \text{ (given) }\end{aligned}$
So,
$b_2=b_3, b_1=b_3+1 and b_1=b_2+1$
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\left(b_3+1\right)+b_3+b_3=1\Rightarrow \quad b_3=0=b_2$ and b_1=1
So,
$\mathbf{b}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}$
Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}, \mathbf{z}$ are three vectors each of magnitude $\sqrt{2}$ and each making an angle $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ with one another. If $\mathbf{a}=\mathbf{x} \times(\mathbf{y} \times \mathbf{z}), \mathbf{b}=\mathbf{y} \times(\mathbf{z} \times \mathbf{x})$, $\mathbf{c}=\mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{y}$, then $\mathbf{x}=$
questions.solution:
Given that, $|\mathbf{x}|=|\mathbf{y}|=|\mathbf{z}|=\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta=60^{{}^{\circ}}$
Thus, $\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{y}=|\mathbf{x}||\mathbf{y}| \cos \theta=(\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{2}) \cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}=2 \times \frac{1}{2}=1$
Similarly $\mathbf{y} \cdot \mathbf{z}=\mathbf{z} \cdot \mathbf{x}=1$
and $\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{x}=|\mathbf{x}||\mathbf{x}| \cos 0^{{}^{\circ}}=(\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{2}) \times 1=2\mathbf{y} \cdot \mathbf{y}=2, \mathbf{z} \cdot \mathbf{z}=2$
Now, $\mathbf{a}=\mathbf{x} \times(\mathbf{y} \times \mathbf{z})=(\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{z}) \mathbf{y}-(\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{y}) \mathbf{z}=1 \cdot y-1 \cdot z\mathbf{a}=\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{z}\ldots(\mathrm{i})$
Also, $\quad \mathbf{b}=\mathbf{y} \times(\mathbf{z} \times \mathbf{x})=(\mathbf{y} \cdot \mathbf{z}) \mathbf{z}-(\mathbf{y} \cdot \mathbf{z}) \mathbf{x}=1 \cdot \mathbf{z}-1 \cdot \mathbf{x}\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x}\ldots(\mathrm{ii})$
Adding Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}=(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{z})+(\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x})y-x=a+b\ldots(\mathrm{iii})$
Again $\quad \mathbf{c}=\mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{y}$
Taking cross product with $\mathbf{x}$ on both sides
$\mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{c}=\mathbf{x} \times(\mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{y})=(\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{y}) \mathbf{x}-(\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{x}) \mathbf{y}\mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{c}=(1) \mathbf{x}-(2) \mathbf{y} \Rightarrow \mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{c}=\mathbf{x}-2 \mathbf{y}\ldots(\mathrm{iv})$
Finally, $\mathbf{c}=\mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{y}$
Taking cross product with $\mathbf{y}$ on both sides
$\mathbf{y} \times \mathbf{c}=\mathbf{y} \times(\mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{y})\mathbf{y} \times \mathbf{c}=(\mathbf{y} \cdot \mathbf{y}) \mathbf{x}-(\mathbf{y} \cdot \mathbf{x}) \mathbf{y}=(2) \mathbf{x}-(1) \mathbf{y}\mathbf{y} \times \mathbf{c}=2 \mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\ldots(v)$
Subtracting Eq. (v) from Eq. (iv), we get $\mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{c}-\mathbf{y} \times \mathbf{c}=(+\mathbf{x}-2 \mathbf{y})-(2 \mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y})(\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}) \times \mathbf{c}=-\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}$ or $\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{y}=(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}) \times \mathbf{c}$
From Eq. (iii), $\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\therefore \quad \mathbf{x}+\mathbf{y}=(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}\ldots(v i)$
Subtracting Eq. (iii) from Eq. (vi), we get
$(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{y})-(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x})=(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}-(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})2 \mathbf{x}=(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}-(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})\mathbf{x}=\frac{1}{2}[(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}-(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})]$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\mathbf{a}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}, \mathbf{b}=-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$. If $\mathbf{c}$ is a vector such that $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}=|\mathbf{c}|,|\mathbf{c}-\mathbf{a}|=2 \sqrt{2}$ and the angle between $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c}$ is $\frac{\pi}{3}$, then $|(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}|=$
questions.solution:
Given, $\mathbf{a}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$, then $|\mathbf{a}|=\sqrt{4+4+1}=3$
Now given $|\mathbf{c}-\mathbf{a}|=2 \sqrt{2}$
Squaring on both sides,
$|\mathbf{c}-\mathbf{a}|^2=8 \Rightarrow|\mathbf{c}|^2+|\mathbf{a}|^2-2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}=8|\mathbf{c}|^2+9-2|\mathbf{c}|=8 \quad[\because|\mathbf{a}|=3$ and $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}=|\mathbf{c}|]\therefore \quad|\mathbf{c}|^2-2|\mathbf{c}|+1=0(|\mathbf{c}|-1)^2=0 \Rightarrow|\mathbf{c}|-1=0 \Rightarrow|\mathbf{c}|=1$
Now, we find $(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b})=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right|(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b})=\hat{\mathbf{i}}(-2+1)-\hat{\mathbf{j}}(2-0)+\hat{\mathbf{k}}(-2)(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b})=-\hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\therefore \quad|\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}|=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3$
Now, given angle between $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c}$ is $\frac{\pi}{3}$.
$\therefore|(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}|=|\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}||\mathbf{c}| \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{3}=3 \times 1 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}$

questions.q: The volume of the tetrahedron (in cubic units) formed by the plane $2 x+y+z=K$ and the coordinate planes is $\frac{2 V^3}{3}$, then $K: V=$
questions.solution:
Equation of given plane is
$2 x+y+z=K$
Point of intersection of plane (i) with the coordinate axes is $A\left(\frac{K}{2}, 0,0\right), B(0, K, 0)$ and $C(0,0, K)$.
Now, volume of the tetrahedron $O A B C\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{6}[\mathbf{O A} \mathbf{O B} \mathbf{O C}]=\frac{1}{6}\left|$\begin{array}{ccc}$\frac{K}{2}$ & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & K & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & K\end{array}$\right|=\frac{2 V^3}{3} \text{ (given) } \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{6} \frac{K^3}{2}=\frac{2 V^3}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{K}{V}\right)^3=2^3 \Rightarrow K: V=2: 1\end{aligned}$
Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q: If the angle between the vectors $2 \alpha^2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \alpha \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $7 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\alpha \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ is obtuse, then
questions.solution: Given vectors$2 \alpha^2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \alpha \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \text{ and } 7 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\alpha \hat{\mathbf{k}}$Angle between these vector are obtuse$\begin{array}{ll}\therefore \cos \theta < 0 & \\& \frac{\left(2 \alpha^2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \alpha \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}\right)(7 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\alpha \hat{\mathbf{k}})}{\left|2 \alpha^2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \alpha \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \| 7 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\alpha \hat{\mathbf{k}}\right|} \\\Rightarrow & 14 \alpha^2-8 \alpha+\alpha < 0 \Rightarrow 14 \alpha^2-7 \alpha < 0 \\\Rightarrow 7 \alpha(2 \alpha-1) < 0 \Rightarrow \alpha \in\left(0, \frac{1}{2}\right) \\\therefore & 0 < \alpha < \frac{1}{2}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The direction ratios of a bisector of the angle between two lines whose direction ratios are $1,1,2$ and $\sqrt{3},-\sqrt{3},$0$ are$
questions.solution:
Let vectors along lines whose direction ratios
are $1,1,2$ and $\sqrt{3},-\sqrt{3},$0$.
\mathbf{a}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{b}=\sqrt{3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}}-\sqrt{3} \hat{\mathbf{j}}\because \mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ have same magnitudes, so the bisector vector of angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are $\pm \mathbf{a} \pm \mathbf{b}= \pm(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \pm(\sqrt{3 \mathbf{i}}-\sqrt{3} \mathbf{j})$
From the options the vector $(1+\sqrt{3}) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(1-\sqrt{3}) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ is correct, means direction ratios of a bisector is $1+\sqrt{3}, 1-\sqrt{3}, 2$. Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.q: Let $a=p(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \cdot \mathbf{b}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{c}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ be three vectors. If the value of [abc] is not more then 15 and not less than -5 , then $P$ lies in the interval
questions.solution:
$We have,
\begin{aligned}
& \mathbf{a}=p \hat{\mathbf{i}}+p \hat{\mathbf{j}}+p \hat{\mathbf{k}}, \mathbf{b}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}, \\
& \mathbf{c}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\
& {[\mathbf{a} \mathbf{b} \mathbf{c}] }=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
p & p & p \\
1 & 1 & -2 \\
2 & -1 & 2
\end{array}\right| \\
&=p(2-2)-p(2+4)+p(-1-2) \\
& \therefore[\mathbf{a b c}]=-9 p \\
& \text{ Given }-5 \leq[\mathbf{a b c}] \leq 15 \\
&-5 \leq-9 p \leq 15 \\
& \therefore \quad-\frac{5}{3} \leq p \leq \frac{5}{9} \\
& p \in\left[\frac{-5}{3}, \frac{5}{9}\right]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\mathbf{a}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{b}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$. If the orthogonal projection vector of $\mathbf{a}$ on $\mathbf{b}$ be $\mathbf{x}$ and the orthogonal projection vector of $\mathbf{b}$ on a be $\mathbf{y}$, then $|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}|=$
questions.solution:
The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ on $\mathbf{b}$ is
$\mathbf{x}=\frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{b}|^2} \mathbf{b}$
And the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{b}$ on $\mathbf{a}$ is
$\mathbf{y}=\frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{a}|^2} \mathbf{a}\therefore \quad \mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}\left(\frac{\mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{b}|^2}-\frac{\mathbf{a}}{|\mathbf{a}|^2}\right)\because \quad \mathbf{a}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{b}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\therefore \quad \mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}=-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}$ and $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=2-2+4=4$
and $|\mathbf{a}|^2=9=|\mathbf{b}|^2\therefore \quad \mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}=(-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}) \frac{4}{9}=\frac{4}{9}(-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}})$
So, $|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}|=\frac{4}{9} \sqrt{10}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\mathbf{a}=2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}, \mathbf{b}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{c}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ are three vectors, then $|(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}|=$
questions.solution: We have,$\begin{gathered} \\ \mathbf{a}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}, \\ \\ \mathbf{b}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ \mathbf{c}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ |(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}|=|(\mathbf{c} \cdot \mathbf{a}) \mathbf{b}-(\mathbf{c} \cdot \mathbf{b}) \mathbf{a}| \\ \\ =|(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}})-(6 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-9 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}})| \\ \\ =|-4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+7 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}|=\sqrt{16+49+1}=\sqrt{66} \\ \\ \text{ and }|\mathbf{a} \times(\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c})=|(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}) \mathbf{b}-(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}) \mathbf{c} \mid \\ \end{gathered} \begin{array}{ll}= & |(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}})-(14 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+7 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+7 \hat{\mathbf{k}})| \\= & |-12 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-9 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}|=\sqrt{144+81+9}=\sqrt{234} \\\Rightarrow & \quad \frac{|(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}|}{\mid \mathbf{a} \times(\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c})}=\sqrt{\frac{66}{234}} \\\Rightarrow & \quad|(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}) \times \mathbf{c}|=\sqrt{\frac{11}{39}}|\mathbf{a} \times(\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c})|\end{array}$

questions.solution: Given,$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathbf{a} & =4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}} \text{$ and $} \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=0 \\ \\ \frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}}{|\mathbf{a}|} & =1, \frac{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{c}}{|\mathbf{b}|}=2 \\ \\ \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} & =0 \\ \\ \therefore \mathbf{b} & =3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \end{aligned}$Let $\mathbf{c}=x \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{y} \begin{aligned} \\ & \therefore \frac{(4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \cdot(x \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{y \hat{\mathrm{j}}})}{5}=1 \\ \\ & =4 x+4 y=5 \\ \end{aligned}$and $\frac{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{c}}{|\mathrm{b}|}=2 \therefore 3 x-4 y=10$On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get$\begin{aligned} \\ & x =2 y=-1 \\ \\ \therefore & \mathbf{c}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathfrak{j}} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $A B C$ be a triangle with $A(\alpha, 5, \beta)$, $B(-2,1,6)$ and $C(1,0,-3)$ as its vertices. If the median through $B$ is equally inclined to the coordinate axes, then $\alpha+\beta=$
questions.solution: We have,A B Cbe a triangle with $vertices\begin{aligned} \\ & A(\alpha, 5, \beta), B(-2,1,6) \text{$ and $} C(1,0,-3) \\ \\ & D=\text{ Mid-point of } A C \\ \\ & \therefore D\left(\frac{\alpha+1}{2}, \frac{5}{2}, \frac{\beta-3}{2}\right) \\ \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} \\ & \mathbf{B D}=\left(\frac{\alpha+1}{2}+2\right) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\left(\frac{5}{2}-1\right) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\left(\frac{\beta-3}{2}-6\right) \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ & \mathbf{B D}=\left(\frac{\alpha+5}{2}\right) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\left(\frac{\beta-15}{2}\right) \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \end{aligned}$BD is equally inclined to the coordinate axis$\begin{aligned} \\ & \therefore\left(\frac{\alpha+5}{2}\right)^2=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2=\left(\frac{\beta-15}{2}\right)^2 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\alpha+5}{2}=\frac{3}{2} \text{$ and $} \frac{\beta-15}{2}=\frac{3}{2} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=-2 \text{ and } \beta=18 \\ \\ & \text{and } \alpha+\beta=-2+18=16 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}$ be a non-zero vector. If $\overset{→}{x} = \overset{^}{i} \times ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{^}{i} ) , \overset{→}{y} = \overset{^}{j} \times ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{^}{j} ) - \overset{→}{a}$ and~$\overset{→}{z} = \overset{^}{k} \times ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{^}{k} ) - \overset{→}{a},$~then $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{x} & \overset{→}{y} & \overset{→}{z}\end{cases}\right] =$
questions.solution:
Given,& $\overset{→}{x} = \overset{^}{i} \times ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{^}{i} ) , \overset{→}{y} = \overset{^}{j} \times ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{^}{j} ) - \overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{z} = \overset{^}{k} \times ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{^}{k} ) - \overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{x} = \left(\overset{^}{i} \cdot \overset{^}{i}\right)\overset{→}{a} - \left(\overset{^}{i} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)\overset{^}{i}, \overset{→}{y} = \left(\overset{^}{j} \cdot \overset{^}{j}\right)\overset{→}{a} - \left(\overset{^}{j} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)\overset{^}{j} - \overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{z} = \left(\overset{^}{k} \cdot \overset{^}{k}\right)\overset{→}{a} - \left(\overset{^}{k} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)\overset{^}{k} - \overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{x} = \overset{→}{a} - \left(\overset{^}{i} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)\overset{^}{i}, \overset{→}{y} = - \left(\overset{^}{j} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)\overset{^}{j}$ and& $\overset{→}{z} = - \left(\overset{^}{k} . \overset{→}{a}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Let, $\overset{→}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$, then $\overset{→}{x} = \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{y} = - \beta\overset{^}{j}$ and& $\overset{→}{z} = - \gamma\overset{^}{k}$.

Now, $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{x} & \overset{→}{y} & \overset{→}{z}\end{cases}\right] = \overset{→}{x} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{y} \times \overset{→}{z}\right)

$⇒ $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{x}$& \overset{→}{y} & \overset{→}{z}\end{cases}\right] = $\left(\beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot\left( \left(- \beta\right)\overset{^}{j} \times \left(- \gamma\right)\overset{^}{k}\right)

$⇒ $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{x}$& \overset{→}{y} & \overset{→}{z}\end{cases}\right] = $\left(\beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\beta\gamma\overset{^}{i}\right) =0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\overset{\to}{r}$ is a unit vector satisfying $\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{b}, | \overset{\to}{a} | = 2$ and $| \overset{\to}{b} | = \sqrt{3},$ then one such $\overset{\to}{r} =$
questions.solution:
Given, $\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ - \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)\overset{\to}{r} + \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{r}\right)\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{r} = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{r}\right)\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) . . . \left(i\right)$

Let, the angle between $\overset{\to}{r}$ and $\overset{\to}{a}$ is $\theta$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|

$⇒ 1 \times 2sin\theta = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \theta = $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Now, $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 1 \times 2cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} =1$

Put, $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 1 in$ the Equation $\left(i\right)$

(i), (ii) and $(iii), we get \\ \begin{aligned}$

\Rightarrow \quad & \quad|$\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$+$\mathbf{c}$|=10 $\sqrt{2}$

questions.q: If $a, b, c$ are distinct real numbers and $P, Q, R$ are three points whose position vectors are respectively $a \hat{\mathbf{i}}+b \hat{\mathbf{j}}+c \hat{\mathbf{k}}, b \hat{\mathbf{i}}+c \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $c \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a \hat{\mathbf{j}}+b \hat{\mathbf{k}}$, then $\angle Q P R=$
questions.solution:
Position vector of $P=a \hat{\mathbf{i}}+b \hat{\mathbf{j}}+c \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Position vector of $Q=b \hat{\mathbf{i}}+c \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Position vector of $R=c \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a \hat{\mathbf{j}}+b \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Now, $\mathbf{P Q}=\mathrm{PV}$ of $Q-\mathrm{PV} of P$
$=(b \hat{\mathbf{i}}+c \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a \hat{\mathbf{k}})-(a \hat{\mathbf{i}}+b \hat{\mathbf{j}}+c \hat{\mathbf{k}})$

$=(b-a) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(c-b) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+(a-c) \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Similarly, $\mathbf{P R}=(c-a) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(a-b) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+(b-c) \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Now, $\mathbf{P Q} \cdot \mathbf{P R}=[(b-a) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(c-b) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+(a-c) \hat{\mathbf{k}}]$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \cdot[(c-a) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(a-b) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+(b-c) \hat{\mathbf{k}}] \\ \\ = & (b-a)(c-a)+(c-b)(a-b)+(a-c)(b-c) \\ \\ = & a^2+b^2+c^2-a b-b c-c a \\ \\ |\mathbf{P Q}|= & \sqrt{(b-a)^2+(c-b)^2+(a-c)^2} \\ \\ |\mathbf{P R}|= & \sqrt{(c-a)^2+(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2} \\ \end{aligned}$
Now, $\cos \theta=\frac{\mathbf{P Q} \cdot \mathbf{P R}}{|\mathbf{P Q}||\mathbf{P R}|}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\frac{a^2+b^2+c^2-a b-b c-c a}{(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2} \\ \\ & =\frac{a^2+b^2+c^2-a b-b c-c a}{2 a^2+2 b^2+2 c^2-2 a b-2 b c-2 c a} \\ \\ & =\frac{a^2+b^2+c^2-a b-b c-c a}{2\left(a^2+b^2+c^2-a b-b c-c a\right)} \\ \\ \cos \theta & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \\ \therefore \quad \theta & =\frac{\pi}{3} \\ \end{aligned}$
Hence, $\angle Q P R=\frac{\pi}{3}$.

questions.solution: Given,$\begin{aligned} \\ A & =(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ \\ B & =(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ \\ C & =\frac{1}{4}(7 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+15 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+15 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ \\ D & =\frac{1}{3}(7 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+(5+3 a) \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ \\ \mathbf{A C} & =\left(\frac{7}{4} \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\frac{15}{4} \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\frac{15}{4} \hat{\mathbf{k}}\right)-(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ \\ \mathbf{A C} & =\frac{3}{4} \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\frac{7}{4} \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\frac{3}{4} \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ \text{and } \mathbf{B D} & =\left(\frac{7}{3} \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\frac{2}{3} \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\left(\frac{5+3 a}{3}\right) \hat{\mathbf{k}}\right)-(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ \\ \mathbf{B D} & =\frac{1}{3} \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\frac{5}{3} \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\left(\frac{3 a-1}{3}\right) \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \end{aligned}$Also given, $\quad|\mathbf{A C}|=|\mathbf{B D}| \begin{aligned} \\ & \because\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2+\left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2+\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2+\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2+\left(\frac{3 a-1}{3}\right)^2 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{9+49+9}{16}=\frac{1+25+(3 a-1)^2}{9} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{67}{16}=\frac{26+(3 a-1)^2}{9} \\ \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 603=416+16(3 a-1)^2 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 16(3 a-1)^2=187 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $|\mathbf{a}|=4,|\mathbf{b}|=5,|\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}|=3$ and $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$, then $\tan ^2 \theta=$
questions.solution:
Given that,
$|\mathbf{a}|=4,|\mathbf{b}|=5,|\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}|=3$
Now, $|\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}|^2=|\mathbf{a}|^2+|\mathbf{b}|^2-2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}$
$\begin{array}{ll} \\ \Rightarrow(3)^2=4^2+5^2-2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} & \Rightarrow 9=16+25-2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} \\ \\ \Rightarrow 2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=32 & \Rightarrow \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=16 \\ \end{array} \\ Now, we know that, \\ $\cos $\theta=\frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{a}| \cdot|\mathbf{b}|}=\frac{16}{4 \cdot 5} \quad \cos \theta=\frac{4}{5} \\ So, $\tan $\theta=\frac{3}{4} \\ $$ \\ $\Rightarrow \quad \tan ^2 $\theta=\frac{9}{16}$

questions.q: If $\mathrm{OA}=6 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{k}}, \mathrm{OB}=2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}$, OC $=5 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ are the coterminous edges of a parallelopiped, then the height of the parallelopiped drawn from the vertex $A$ is
questions.solution:
We have,
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathbf{O A} & =6 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ \mathbf{O B} & =2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ \mathbf{O C} & =5 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ \mathbf{O A} \cdot(\mathbf{O B} \times \mathbf{O C}) & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \\ 6 & 3 & -4 \\ \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ \\ 5 & -1 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right| \\ \\ & =6(4+1)-3(-5)-4(-10) \\ \\ \mathbf{O A} \cdot(\mathbf{O B} \times \mathbf{O C}) & =30+15+40=85 \\ \\ \mathbf{O B} \times \mathbf{O C} & =\left|\begin{array}{lll} \\ 1 & 5 & k \\ \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ \\ 5 & -1 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right|=5 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-10 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ |\mathbf{O B} \times \mathbf{O C}| & =\sqrt{25+25+100}=5 \sqrt{6} \\ \end{aligned}$
Height of parallelopiped drawn from A$
=\frac{\mathrm{OA} \cdot(\mathrm{OB} \times \mathrm{OC})}{|\mathrm{OB} \times \mathrm{OC}|}=\frac{85}{5 \sqrt{6}}=\frac{17}{\sqrt{6}}$

questions.solution:
If $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right|$
$=\hat{\mathbf{i}}(3-6)-\hat{\mathbf{j}}(6+3)+\hat{\mathbf{k}}(-4-1)=-3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-9 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-5 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
and $\mathbf{c} \times \mathbf{d}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \mathbf{k} \\ -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right|$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The vector that is parallel to the vector $2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$ and coplanar with the vectors $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is
questions.solution:
Let& the required vector is $a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}$.

As the three vectors $a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar so one must be linear combination of other two& i.e,
$a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k} = \lambda \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right) + \mu\left(\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)

$⇒ a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + $\left(\lambda + \mu\right)\left(\overset{^}{j}\right)$+ \mu\overset{^}{k}

On comparison, we get

$ a = \lambda, c = \mu & b = \lambda + \mu ⇒ b = a + c$

Also, $a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}$ is parallel to $2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$.

So, $a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k} = \alpha \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right)

$⇒ a = 2\alpha,$ b = - $2\alpha$& c = - $4\alpha$⇒ b = a + c$

Only option $\left(b\right)$\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ has $a = 1, b = - 1, c = - 2$ such that $a + c = 1 - 2 = - 1 = b ⇒ b = a + c

So, the $required vector is \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The volume of a tetrahedron whose vertices are $4\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, 3\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ and $- 2\overset{^}{i} + 4j + 4\overset{^}{k}$ is (in cubic units)
questions.solution:
Let the given vertices be&

$P = 4\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$Q = - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$R = 3\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

$S = - 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{PQ} = \overset{→}{OQ} - \overset{→}{OP}$

$= \left(0 - 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(- 1 - 5\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(1 - 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$= - 4\overset{^}{i} - 6\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{PR} = \overset{→}{OR} - \overset{→}{OP}$

$= \left(3 - 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(9 - 5\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(4 - 1\right)\overset{^}{k} = - \overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{PS} = \overset{→}{OS} - \overset{→}{OP}$

$= \left(- 2 - 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(4 - 5\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(4 - 1\right)\overset{^}{k} = - 6\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Volume of tetrahedron$= \dfrac{1}{6} \times$ Volume of parallelepiped

Volume of parallelepiped$= \left[\overset{→}{PQ}, \overset{→}{PR}, \overset{→}{PS}\right]

$= $\left| \begin{cases}-4 & - 6 & 0 \\ - 1 & 4 & 3 \\ - 6 & - 1 & 3\end{cases} \right|

$= - 4 $\left(12 + 3\right) + 6 \left(-3 + 18\right)$

$= - 60 + 90$

$= 30$ cubic units

Therefore, volume of tetrahedron$= \dfrac{1}{6} \times30 = 5$& cubic units.

questions.q: If $\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{b}$ and $\overline{\mathbf{c}}$ are three vectors with magnitudes 1,1 and 2 respectively and $\mathbf{a} \times(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{c})+\mathbf{b}=0$, then the angle between $a$ and $c$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& |\mathbf{a}|=1|\mathbf{b}|=1 \quad|\mathbf{c}|=2 \\
& \mathbf{a} \times(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{c})+\mathbf{b}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathbf{a} \times(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{c})=-\mathbf{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad[\mathbf{a} \times(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{c})]^2=\mathbf{b}^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad[(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}) \mathbf{a}-(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{a}) \mathbf{c}]^2=\mathbf{b}^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad\left[(a c \cos \theta) \mathbf{a}-\mathbf{a}^2 \cdot \mathbf{c}\right]^2=b^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad[2 \cdot \cos \theta \cdot \mathbf{a}-\mathbf{c}]^2=b^2 \\
& \Rightarrow 4 \cos ^2 \theta \cdot a^2+c^2-4 \cos \theta \cdot \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 4 \cos ^2 \theta+4-4 \cos ^2 \theta \cdot 1 \cdot 2=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad-4 \cos ^2 \theta=-3 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \cos ^2 \theta=\frac{3}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \cos \theta=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\pi}{6} \\
&
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A vector $\overset{→}{a}$ of length $2$ units is making an angle $60 °$ with each of the $X$-axis and $Y$-axis. If another vector $\overset{→}{b}$ of length $\sqrt{2} units is making an angle 45 °$ with each of the $Y$-axis and $Z$-axis, then \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} =
questions.solution:
Let, $\overset{→}{a}$ makes an angle $\theta$ with $Z$-axis and $\overset{→}{b}$ makes an angle $ϕ$ from $X$-axis.

Apply $\cos^{2}60 ° + \cos^{2}60 ° + \cos^{2}\theta = 1 \text{ and } \cos^{2}ϕ + \cos^{2}45 ° + \cos^{2}45 ° = 1$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{\pm 1}{2} \text{ and } cosϕ = 0$

So, $\overset{→}{a} = \left(2cos{60}^{∘}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2cos{60}^{∘}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2cos\theta\right)\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \left(\sqrt{2}cosϕ\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(\sqrt{2}cos{45}^{∘}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(\sqrt{2}cos{45}^{∘}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} \pm \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Now, $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & \pm \sqrt{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left(1 \pm \sqrt{2}\right)\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

questions.q: If $\overset{¯}{OA} = \overset{¯}{i} + 2\overset{¯}{j} + 3\overset{¯}{k}$ and $\overset{¯}{OB} = 4\overset{¯}{i} + \overset{¯}{k}$ are the position vectors of the points $A$ and $B$, then the position vector of a point on the line passing through $B$ and parallel to the vector $\overset{¯}{OA} \times \overset{¯}{OB}$ which is at a distance of $\sqrt{189} units from $B$ is$
questions.solution:
Let, $C = \left(x, y, z\right) such that $\overset{→}{BC}$ is parallel to $\overset{→}{OA} \times \overset{→}{OB} and $\left|\overset{→}{BC}\right|$ =\sqrt{189}.

Apply \overset{→}{BC} = \lambda\overset{→}{OA} \times \overset{→}{OB}$

$⇒ $\left(x - 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + \left(z - 1\right)\overset{^}{k} = \$ lambda $\left| \begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{cases} \right|

$⇒ $\left(x - 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + \left(z - 1\right)\overset{^}{k} = \$ lambda $\left[2\overset{^}{i} + 11\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}\right]$

$⇒ x = 4 + 2\lambda, y = 11\lambda, z = 1 - 8\lambda$

Apply $\left|\overset{→}{BC}\right| =\sqrt{189}

$⇒ \sqrt{$\left(2\lambda\right)^{2} + \left(11\lambda\right)^{2} + \left(- 8\lambda\right)^{2}} = \sqrt{189}

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

So the position vector of the point $C$ is 6\overset{^}{i} + 11\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}$.

questions.q: If the vectors $\overset{→}{b}, \overset{→}{c}, \overset{→}{d}$ are not coplanar, then, the vector $\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)\times \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d}\right)+ \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)\times \left(\overset{→}{d} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)+ \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{d}\right)\times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)is$

$⇒ [ \overset{→}{a} \cdot ( \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d} ) ] \overset{→}{b} - [ \overset{→}{b} \cdot ( \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d} ) ] \overset{→}{a} + [ \overset{→}{a} \cdot ( \overset{→}{d} \times \overset{→}{b} ) ] \overset{→}{c} - [ \overset{→}{c} \cdot ( \overset{→}{d} \times \overset{→}{d} ) ] \overset{→}{a} + [ \overset{→}{a} \cdot ( \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} ) ]$d - [ \overset{→}{d} $\cdot ( \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} ) ] \overset{→}{a}

$⇒ [ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{c}\overset{→}{d} ] \overset{→}{b} - [ \overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{c}\overset{→}{d} ] \overset{→}{a} + [ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{d}\overset{→}{b} ] \overset{→}{c} - [ \overset{→}{c}\overset{→}{d}\overset{→}{b} ] \overset{→}{a} + [ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{c} ] \overset{→}{d} - $\left[\overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{c}\right]$\overset{→}{a}$\left(∴ \overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)$ = $\left[\overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{c}\right]$\right)

questions.q: If $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are wit vectors and $\alpha$ is the angle between them, then $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ is a wnit vector when $\cos \alpha=$
questions.solution:
We have, $|\mathbf{a}|=|\mathbf{b}|=1$ and $\alpha$ is the angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$.
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \text{Clearly, } \cos \alpha=\frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \cos \alpha=\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} \\ \end{aligned}$
Now, let $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ is a unit vector, then
$\begin{aligned} \\ & |\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|=1 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|^2=1 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad\langle\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\rangle \cdot\langle\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\rangle=1 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}+\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}=1 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad|\mathbf{a}|^2+2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}+|\mathbf{b}|^2=1 \quad[\because \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}] \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 1+2 \cos \alpha+1=1 \quad \text{ [using Eq. (i)] } \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 1+2 \cos \alpha=0 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \cos \alpha=-\frac{1}{2} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
We have, $|\mathbf{a}|=3,|\mathbf{b}|=4$ and $|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|=5$
Since,
$\begin{gathered} \\ |\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|=5 \\ \\ |\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|^2=25 \\ \end{gathered}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \therefore \quad|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|^2=25 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\rangle \cdot(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\rangle=25 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}=25 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad|\mathbf{a}|^2+2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}+|\mathbf{b}|^2=25 \quad[\because \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}] \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 9+2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}+16=25 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=0 \\ \end{aligned}$
Now, consider $|\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}|^2=(\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b})(\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b})$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{a}-\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b} \\ \\ & =|\mathbf{a}|^2-2 \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}+|\mathbf{b}|^2 \quad[\because \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}] \\ \\ & =9-0+16=25 \\ \\ \Rightarrow \mid \mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b} & =5 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The shortest distance between the skew lines $\hat{\mathbf{r}}=(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}})+t(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}})$ and $\hat{\mathbf{r}}=(4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+6 \hat{\mathbf{k}})+t(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}})$ is
questions.solution:
Given skew lines are
$\mathbf{r}=(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}})+t(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}})$
and $\mathrm{r}=(4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+6 \hat{\mathbf{k}})+t(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}})$
Here,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathbf{a}_1=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \\ & \mathrm{b}_1=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ & \mathrm{a}_2=4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+6 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ & \mathrm{b}_2=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \end{aligned}$
and
$\mathbf{b}_2=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Now, 0
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathbf{a}_2-\mathbf{a}_1 & =4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+6 \hat{\mathbf{k}}-(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ \\ & =3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \end{aligned}$
and
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathrm{b}_1 \times \mathrm{b}_2 & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \\ \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ \end{array}\right| \\ \\ & =\hat{\mathbf{i}}(3-6)-\hat{\mathbf{j}}(1-4)+\hat{\mathbf{k}}(3-6) \\ \\ & =-3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ The shortest distance between skew lines
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\frac{\left|\left(\mathbf{a}_2-\mathbf{a}_1\right) \cdot\left(\mathbf{b}_1 \times \mathbf{b}_2\right)\right|}{\left|\mathbf{b}_1 \times \mathbf{b}_2\right|} \\ \\ & =\frac{|(3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \cdot(-3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{k}})|}{\sqrt{(-3)^2+(3)^2+(-3)^2}} \\ \\ & =\frac{|-9+9-9|}{\sqrt{9+9+9}}=\frac{9}{3 \sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\hat{\mathbf{a}}, \hat{\mathbf{b}}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{c}}$ are vectors with magnitudes 2,3 and 4 respectively, then the best upper bound of $|\hat{\mathbf{a}}-\hat{\mathbf{b}}|^2+|\hat{\mathbf{b}}-\hat{\mathbf{c}}|^2+|\hat{\mathbf{c}}-\hat{\mathbf{a}}|^2$ among the given values is
questions.solution:
Given, $|\mathrm{a}|=2,|\mathrm{ b}|=3$ and $|\mathrm{c}|=4$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \begin{aligned} \\ & \therefore|a-b|^2+|b-c|^2+|c-a|^2 \\ \\ &= a^2+b^2-2 a \cdot b+b^2+c^2-2 b \cdot c \\ \\ & \quad+c^2+a^2-2 a \cdot c \\ \\ &= 2\left(a^2+b^2+c^2\right)-2(a \cdot b+b \cdot c+c \cdot a) \\ \\ & \begin{array}{rl} \\ 2 & 2(a \cdot b+b \cdot c+c \cdot a) \\ \end{array} \\ \\ &=2 \left(a^2+b^2+c^2\right) \\ \\ & \quad-\left(|a-b|^2+|b-c|^2+|c-a|^2\right) \\ \end{aligned} \\ \end{aligned}$
We know, $(a+b+c)^2 \geq 0$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \therefore \quad a^2+b^2+c^2+2(a \cdot b+b \cdot c+c \cdot a) \geq 0 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad a^2+b^2+c^2+2 \left(a^2+b^2+c^2\right) \\ \\ & -\left(|a-b|^2+|b-c|^2+|c-a|^2\right) \geq 0 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}|^2+|\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c}|^2+|\mathrm{c}-\mathrm{a}|^2 \\ \\ & \leq 3 \left(a^2+b^2+c^2\right) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow|a-b|^2+|b-c|^2+|c-a|^2 \\ \\ & \leq 3 \left(2^2+3^2+4^2\right) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow|a-b|^2+|b-c|^2+|c-a|^2 \\ \\ & \leq 3(4+9+16) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow|a-b|^2+|b-c|^2+|c-a|^2 \leq 87 \\ \end{aligned}$

$\mathbf{a}=\sin ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\cos ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$, where $x \in R$.
If pairs of vectors $\mathbf{a}, \hat{\mathbf{i}}, \mathbf{a}, \hat{\mathbf{j}} ; \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{k}$ are adjacent sides of 3 parallelogram
Area of 1st parallelogram $=|\mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}}|$
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}} & =\left(\sin ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\cos ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}\right) \times \hat{\mathbf{i}} \\ \\ & =0+\cos ^2 x(\hat{\mathbf{j}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}})+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}} \\ \\ & =-\cos ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{k}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \\ |\mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}}| & =\sqrt{\cos ^4 x+1} \\ \end{aligned}$
Now, area of 2nd parallelogram $=|\mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}}|$
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}} & =\left(\sin ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\cos ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}\right) \times \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \\ & =\sin ^2 x(\hat{\mathbf{i}} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}})+0+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \\ & =\sin ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{k}}-\hat{\mathbf{i}} \\ \\ \therefore \mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}} & =\sqrt{\sin ^4 x+1} \\ \end{aligned}$
Now, area 3rd parallelogram $|\mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}}|$
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}} & =\left(\sin ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\cos ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}\right) \times \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ & =\sin ^2 x(\hat{\mathbf{i}} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}})+\cos ^2 x(\hat{\mathbf{j}} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}})+0 \\ \\ & =-\sin ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\cos ^2 x \hat{\mathbf{i}} \\ \end{aligned}$
$|\mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}}|=\sqrt{\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x}$
Now, sum of areas
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =|\mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}}|^2+|\mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}}|^2+|\mathbf{a} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}}|^2 \\ \\ & =\cos ^4 x+1+\sin ^4 x+1+\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x \\ \\ & =2+2\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) \\ \\ & \left.=2+2\left\{\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right)^2-2 \sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x\right)\right\} \\ \\ A & =2+2\left(1-\frac{1}{2}(\sin 2 x)^2\right) \\ \\ A & =2+2-(\sin 2 x)^2=4-(\sin 2 x)^2 \\ \end{aligned}$
We know that,
$-1 \leq \sin 2 x \leq 1$
So, $0 \leq(\sin 2 x)^2 \leq 1$
So, $3 \leq A \leq 4$
Hence, $A$ lies in $[3,4]$.
